longissimus_thoracis.title: Longissimus thoracis
longissimus_thoracis.overview: The thoracic part of the middle longitudinal epaxial muscle system. It is continuous with neighboring longissimus regions.
longissimus_thoracis.location: Dorsolateral thoracic vertebral column, medial to iliocostalis and lateral to the transversospinal system.
longissimus_thoracis.attachments: Vertebral processes and associated thoracolumbar connective tissue to more cranial vertebral/rib attachments through overlapping fascicles.
longissimus_thoracis.function: Bilateral activity supports spinal extension; unilateral activity contributes to lateral bending and segmental stabilization.
longissimus_thoracis.nerve: Dorsal branches of thoracic spinal nerves.
longissimus_thoracis.physio: Learn an overlapping system rather than imagining one long tendon between two points. A surface mesh cannot reveal individual fascicle activation.
longissimus_thoracis.recall: Which two epaxial systems border longissimus?

longissimus_lumborum.title: Longissimus lumborum
longissimus_lumborum.overview: The lumbar portion of longissimus, forming a substantial part of the dorsal trunk musculature.
longissimus_lumborum.location: Along the dorsolateral lumbar spine, deep to thoracolumbar fascia.
longissimus_lumborum.attachments: Iliac and sacral/vertebral connective-tissue origins connect through fascicles to lumbar and more cranial vertebral processes.
longissimus_lumborum.function: Extends and stabilizes the lumbar region; asymmetric activity contributes to lateral bending.
longissimus_lumborum.nerve: Dorsal branches of lumbar spinal nerves.
longissimus_lumborum.physio: Distinguish the muscle from its overlying fascia and from the ventral psoas muscles. Size alone does not establish strength or spinal stability.
longissimus_lumborum.recall: Is this muscle epaxial or hypaxial, and how does that predict its nerve supply?

longissimus_cervicis.title: Longissimus cervicis
longissimus_cervicis.overview: The cervical continuation of the longissimus system, with several overlapping attachments.
longissimus_cervicis.location: Dorsolateral cervical region, deep to superficial neck muscles.
longissimus_cervicis.attachments: Cranial thoracic vertebral processes to transverse processes of cervical vertebrae.
longissimus_cervicis.function: Extends the neck bilaterally and bends it toward the active side unilaterally.
longissimus_cervicis.nerve: Dorsal branches of cervical and adjacent thoracic spinal nerves.
longissimus_cervicis.physio: Neck motion is shared across muscles and joints; do not interpret the source’s merged surface as a single isolated segmental actuator.
longissimus_cervicis.recall: How does its position differ from longus capitis?

longissimus_capitis.title: Longissimus capitis
longissimus_capitis.overview: A long epaxial muscle connecting cervical/thoracic origins to the skull.
longissimus_capitis.location: Dorsolateral neck, deep to splenius and near the cranial continuation of longissimus cervicis.
longissimus_capitis.attachments: Cervical/cranial thoracic vertebral process region to mastoid part of the temporal bone.
longissimus_capitis.function: Extends the head and neck and contributes to ipsilateral lateral bending.
longissimus_capitis.physio: Separate capitis, which reaches the head, from cervicis, which terminates on cervical vertebrae.
longissimus_capitis.recall: What does the suffix capitis tell you about the terminal attachment?

splenius.title: Splenius
splenius.overview: A broad superficial epaxial neck muscle that helps support and orient the head.
splenius.location: Dorsolateral neck, deep to superficial extrinsic forelimb muscles and superficial to deeper epaxial muscles.
splenius.attachments: Cranial thoracic spinous region and dorsal cervical raphe to caudal skull/nuchal and mastoid regions.
splenius.function: Extends the head and neck; unilateral activity turns or bends the head toward that side.
splenius.nerve: Dorsal branches of cervical spinal nerves.
splenius.physio: Compare broad splenius fibers with the smaller segmental muscles around atlas and axis.
splenius.recall: Why can bilateral and unilateral contractions produce different movements?

longus_capitis.title: Longus capitis
longus_capitis.overview: A deep hypaxial muscle on the ventral side of the cervical spine.
longus_capitis.location: Ventrolateral cervical vertebrae, deep to the airway, esophagus and superficial neck muscles.
longus_capitis.attachments: Cervical transverse process region to the basilar occipital bone.
longus_capitis.function: Flexes and stabilizes the head/cranial neck.
longus_capitis.nerve: Ventral branches of cervical spinal nerves.
longus_capitis.physio: The ventral location contrasts with epaxial extensors. Deep location and nearby vital structures make this an orientation lesson, not a direct-pressure target.
longus_capitis.recall: What determines the hypaxial classification more reliably than a surface view?

rectus_capitis_dorsalis_major.title: Rectus capitis dorsalis major
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_major.overview: A short suboccipital extensor spanning axis to skull.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_major.location: Dorsal cranial neck, deeper than broad superficial extensors.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_major.attachments: Spinous process of axis to caudal occipital region.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_major.function: Extends the head and contributes to fine craniocervical positioning.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_major.nerve: Dorsal branches of the first cervical spinal nerves.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_major.physio: Study it alongside atlas, axis and the occiput; the neck contains two specialized cranial joints with different mechanics.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_major.recall: Which vertebra gives this muscle its caudal attachment?

rectus_capitis_dorsalis_minor.title: Rectus capitis dorsalis minor
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_minor.overview: A small deep muscle connecting atlas directly to the skull.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_minor.location: Immediately dorsal to the atlanto-occipital region, deep to larger suboccipital muscles.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_minor.attachments: Dorsal arch of atlas to occipital bone.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_minor.function: Extends and steadies the head at the atlanto-occipital region.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_minor.nerve: Dorsal branch of the first cervical spinal nerve.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_minor.physio: Its short span favors local positioning rather than large trunk movement. Small size does not imply an unimportant sensory role.
rectus_capitis_dorsalis_minor.recall: How does its vertebral attachment differ from dorsalis major?

rectus_capitis_lateralis.title: Rectus capitis lateralis
rectus_capitis_lateralis.overview: A short lateral connection between atlas and the base of the skull.
rectus_capitis_lateralis.location: Lateral to the atlanto-occipital joint, adjacent to other deep cranial-neck muscles.
rectus_capitis_lateralis.attachments: Atlas wing region to the jugular process of the occipital bone.
rectus_capitis_lateralis.function: Bends the head laterally and helps stabilize the cranial neck.
rectus_capitis_lateralis.nerve: Ventral branch of the first cervical spinal nerve.
rectus_capitis_lateralis.physio: Use the atlas wing as the orientation landmark, while recognizing that the model does not display every nearby vessel or nerve.
rectus_capitis_lateralis.recall: What distinguishes a lateral head positioner from a long cervical extensor?

rectus_capitis_ventr.title: Rectus capitis ventralis
rectus_capitis_ventr.overview: A short ventral suboccipital muscle connecting atlas and skull.
rectus_capitis_ventr.location: Ventral to the atlanto-occipital joint and dorsal to the pharyngeal region.
rectus_capitis_ventr.attachments: Ventral atlas region to basilar occipital bone.
rectus_capitis_ventr.function: Flexes and stabilizes the head at the atlanto-occipital joint.
rectus_capitis_ventr.nerve: Ventral branch of the first cervical spinal nerve.
rectus_capitis_ventr.physio: Contrast the ventral line of pull with that of the dorsal rectus muscles rather than transferring human neck terminology.
rectus_capitis_ventr.recall: Which dorsal muscle also connects atlas directly to the occiput?

obliquus_capitis_caudalis.title: Obliquus capitis caudalis
obliquus_capitis_caudalis.overview: A deep oblique muscle between the first two cervical vertebrae.
obliquus_capitis_caudalis.location: Dorsolateral atlanto-axial region, extending laterally from the axis spine.
obliquus_capitis_caudalis.attachments: Spinous process of axis to wing of atlas.
obliquus_capitis_caudalis.function: Rotates atlas and the head around the dens of axis; also contributes to local stability.
obliquus_capitis_caudalis.nerve: Dorsal cervical spinal branches, chiefly the second cervical nerve.
obliquus_capitis_caudalis.physio: This muscle does not insert on the skull. Its action is understood through the specialized pivot between atlas and axis.
obliquus_capitis_caudalis.recall: Which bony projection forms the atlanto-axial pivot?

obliquus_capitis_cranialis.title: Obliquus capitis cranialis
obliquus_capitis_cranialis.overview: A short oblique muscle connecting atlas to the occipital region.
obliquus_capitis_cranialis.location: Lateral/dorsal atlanto-occipital region, cranial to the caudal oblique muscle.
obliquus_capitis_cranialis.attachments: Wing of atlas to the occipital bone near the nuchal region.
obliquus_capitis_cranialis.function: Extends the head bilaterally and contributes to lateral head positioning unilaterally.
obliquus_capitis_cranialis.nerve: Dorsal branch of the first cervical spinal nerve.
obliquus_capitis_cranialis.physio: Distinguish cranialis from caudalis by whether the muscle reaches the skull. Multiple pieces do not necessarily represent extra muscles.
obliquus_capitis_cranialis.recall: Which of the two oblique capitis muscles reaches the occiput?

sternocephalicus.title: Sternocephalicus
sternocephalicus.overview: A superficial ventral/lateral neck muscle linking the sternum to the head; the model can combine its portions.
sternocephalicus.location: Ventrolateral neck beside the jugular groove and superficial to deeper neck structures.
sternocephalicus.attachments: Manubrial region to caudal skull attachments through its occipital/mastoid portions.
sternocephalicus.function: Flexes the head/neck bilaterally and helps turn the head with unilateral action.
sternocephalicus.nerve: Accessory nerve and cervical spinal contributions.
sternocephalicus.physio: Neck posture can affect superficial contours; the jugular groove is a relationship landmark rather than a place for forceful pressure.
sternocephalicus.recall: Which attachment explains the sterno- prefix?

sternohyroideus.title: Sternohyoideus · corrected source spelling
sternohyroideus.overview: A slender ventral strap muscle connecting sternum and hyoid apparatus. The source spelling is nonstandard.
sternohyroideus.location: Ventral to the trachea, near the midline and paired with its opposite-side counterpart.
sternohyroideus.attachments: Manubrium/first costal region to basihyoid bone.
sternohyroideus.function: Retracts the hyoid apparatus and helps coordinate swallowing-related positioning.
sternohyroideus.nerve: Cervical spinal motor fibers to the infrahyoid muscles.
sternohyroideus.physio: This is a swallowing/hyoid structure, not a primary spinal flexor or an appropriate generic neck-strengthening target.
sternohyroideus.recall: Does it insert on a cervical vertebra or on the hyoid apparatus?

sternothyroideus.title: Sternothyroideus
sternothyroideus.overview: A ventral neck strap muscle that ends on the larynx.
sternothyroideus.location: Along the ventrolateral trachea, deep/adjacent to sternohyoideus.
sternothyroideus.attachments: Manubrial region to thyroid cartilage of the larynx.
sternothyroideus.function: Retracts the larynx during swallowing-related movement.
sternothyroideus.physio: Distinguish thyroid cartilage from the thyroid gland. The name does not mean the muscle controls endocrine function.
sternothyroideus.recall: Which infrahyoid muscle ends on the hyoid rather than thyroid cartilage?

dorsi_scaleni_dors.title: Scalenus · dorsal source portion
dorsi_scaleni_dors.overview: A source-labeled portion of the scalene group; the complete canine group has multiple slips.
dorsi_scaleni_dors.location: Lateral caudal neck and cranial thorax, ventral to portions of serratus ventralis.
dorsi_scaleni_dors.attachments: Cervical transverse process region to cranial ribs; exact slip boundaries are not resolved by the abbreviated model label.
dorsi_scaleni_dors.function: Helps stabilize/flex the neck and can assist inspiration by influencing cranial ribs.
dorsi_scaleni_dors.nerve: Ventral branches of cervical and cranial thoracic spinal nerves.
dorsi_scaleni_dors.physio: Consider the link between neck position and thoracic movement without equating accessory respiratory activity with a diagnosis.
dorsi_scaleni_dors.recall: What two body regions does this muscle connect?

serratus_dorsalis_cranialis.title: Serratus dorsalis cranialis
serratus_dorsalis_cranialis.overview: A thin dorsal thoracic muscle associated with inspiratory rib motion.
serratus_dorsalis_cranialis.location: Superficial to portions of epaxial musculature and deep to large extrinsic trunk/limb muscles.
serratus_dorsalis_cranialis.attachments: Cranial thoracolumbar fascial region to cranial borders of several ribs.
serratus_dorsalis_cranialis.function: Draws ribs cranially and assists expansion of the thoracic wall.
serratus_dorsalis_cranialis.physio: Contrast it with serratus ventralis, whose central role is trunk suspension rather than the same rib action.
serratus_dorsalis_cranialis.recall: Which serratus group forms the major muscular forelimb sling?

serratus_dorsalis_caudalis.title: Serratus dorsalis caudalis
serratus_dorsalis_caudalis.overview: A caudal dorsal thoracic muscle represented by several source slips.
serratus_dorsalis_caudalis.location: Caudodorsal thorax, over the epaxial region and beneath more superficial coverings.
serratus_dorsalis_caudalis.attachments: Thoracolumbar fascia to caudal borders of the last ribs.
serratus_dorsalis_caudalis.function: Draws caudal ribs caudally and assists expiratory thoracic-wall motion.
serratus_dorsalis_caudalis.physio: Source numbers identify mesh slips, not independent muscles with separate functions. Compare its fiber direction with the cranial serratus dorsalis.
serratus_dorsalis_caudalis.recall: Which rib border does this group approach?

intercostals_ext.title: External intercostal muscles
intercostals_ext.overview: Segmental muscles linking adjacent ribs and reinforcing the thoracic wall.
intercostals_ext.location: Outer muscular layer within intercostal spaces, superficial to internal intercostals.
intercostals_ext.attachments: Caudal border of one rib to cranial border of the next through caudoventrally oriented fibers.
intercostals_ext.function: Stabilize rib spaces and generally contribute to inspiration as the ribs are drawn cranially.
intercostals_ext.physio: Rib movement and spinal posture interact, but visible ribs and muscles alone cannot quantify breathing effort.
intercostals_ext.recall: How does the fiber direction compare with the internal layer?

intercostals_int.title: Internal intercostal muscles
intercostals_int.overview: A deeper intercostal layer with fibers crossing the external layer’s direction.
intercostals_int.location: Between neighboring ribs, deep to external intercostals and outside the pleural lining.
intercostals_int.attachments: Adjacent rib borders through generally cranioventrally directed fibers.
intercostals_int.function: Stabilize intercostal spaces and contribute to expiration; action varies with region and mechanical context.
intercostals_int.physio: Avoid treating all intercostal fibers as identical respiratory actuators; the model groups many segments.
intercostals_int.recall: What structures lie deeper than the intercostal wall?

rectus_thoracis.title: Rectus thoracis
rectus_thoracis.overview: A small ventral thoracic-wall muscle near the cranial ribs.
rectus_thoracis.location: Cranial ventrolateral thorax, extending from the first rib toward more caudal costal cartilage.
rectus_thoracis.attachments: First rib region to costal cartilages of the following cranial ribs.
rectus_thoracis.function: Assists movement and stabilization of the cranial thoracic wall during respiration.
rectus_thoracis.physio: Distinguish this short thoracic muscle from rectus abdominis, which spans the ventral abdomen.
rectus_thoracis.recall: Which body cavity lies deep to rectus thoracis?

transverses_thoracis.title: Transversus thoracis
transverses_thoracis.overview: A deep muscle on the internal ventral thoracic wall; the source uses a nonstandard spelling.
transverses_thoracis.location: Inside the rib cage, on the dorsal face of sternum and medial surfaces of costal cartilages.
transverses_thoracis.function: Assists expiration by drawing ventral rib/cartilage structures inward and supports the thoracic wall.
transverses_thoracis.physio: Its internal location explains why an external palpation lesson should not imply direct access to this muscle.
transverses_thoracis.recall: Is this muscle superficial or deep to the sternum?

diaphragma.title: Diaphragm
diaphragma.overview: The main inspiratory muscle and the muscular partition between thoracic and abdominal cavities.
diaphragma.location: Dome-shaped caudal boundary of the thorax; muscular periphery surrounds a central tendon.
diaphragma.attachments: Lumbar crura, internal caudal ribs and sternal region converge on the central tendon.
diaphragma.function: Contraction flattens the dome and increases thoracic volume; it also contributes to abdominal-pressure control.
diaphragma.physio: Posture and breathing interact, but the static model cannot show ventilation or diagnose respiratory dysfunction.
diaphragma.recall: How does flattening the dome change thoracic volume?

obliquus_ext_abdominis.title: External abdominal oblique
obliquus_ext_abdominis.location: Lateral abdomen, superficial to internal oblique and transversus; fibers run generally caudoventrally.
obliquus_ext_abdominis.attachments: Caudal ribs and thoracolumbar fascia to linea alba and pelvic/inguinal connective-tissue attachments.
obliquus_ext_abdominis.function: Compresses/supports abdominal contents, assists forced expiration and contributes to trunk bending and rotation.
obliquus_ext_abdominis.nerve: Ventral thoracic and lumbar spinal branches.
obliquus_ext_abdominis.physio: Study trunk support as coordinated activity across the abdominal wall, not an isolated universal core muscle.
obliquus_ext_abdominis.recall: What midline connective-tissue structure receives its aponeurosis?

obliquus_int_abdominis.title: Internal abdominal oblique
obliquus_int_abdominis.overview: The middle broad muscular layer of the lateral abdominal wall.
obliquus_int_abdominis.location: Deep to external oblique and superficial to transversus; fibers generally run cranioventrally.
obliquus_int_abdominis.attachments: Thoracolumbar/iliac and inguinal region to caudal ribs and linea alba.
obliquus_int_abdominis.function: Compresses abdominal contents and contributes to trunk flexion, rotation and respiratory pressure control.
obliquus_int_abdominis.nerve: Ventral thoracic and lumbar spinal branches.
obliquus_int_abdominis.physio: Compare crossing fiber directions of the two obliques and how they can stabilize as well as move the trunk.
obliquus_int_abdominis.recall: Which abdominal muscle lies deeper than this layer?

tranversus_abdominis.title: Transversus abdominis
tranversus_abdominis.overview: The deepest broad abdominal-wall muscle; the source omits a letter in transversus.
tranversus_abdominis.location: Deep to internal oblique, with fibers oriented predominantly across the abdominal wall.
tranversus_abdominis.attachments: Inner caudal costal region and lumbar transverse-process/fascial attachments to linea alba.
tranversus_abdominis.function: Compresses abdominal contents and contributes to coordinated trunk and abdominal-pressure support.
tranversus_abdominis.nerve: Ventral thoracic and lumbar spinal branches.
tranversus_abdominis.physio: Its transverse course emphasizes support and compression rather than a large isolated spinal bending moment.
tranversus_abdominis.recall: What separates this muscular layer from the abdominal cavity?

rectus_abdominis.title: Rectus abdominis
rectus_abdominis.overview: A paired longitudinal muscle within the rectus sheath of the ventral abdominal wall.
rectus_abdominis.location: On either side of the linea alba, interrupted by tendinous intersections.
rectus_abdominis.attachments: Pubic region to ventral cranial costal cartilages/sternum.
rectus_abdominis.function: Flexes the trunk and supports/compresses the abdominal contents.
rectus_abdominis.nerve: Ventral thoracic and lumbar spinal branches.
rectus_abdominis.physio: Distinguish the muscle belly from the enclosing aponeurotic sheath; the model may not display every intersection separately.
rectus_abdominis.recall: Which midline structure separates the left and right rectus muscles?

levator_caudae_brevis.title: Short dorsal tail-muscle portions
levator_caudae_brevis.overview: The source uses a functional levator caudae label for short dorsal tail-muscle slips. It is not a complete modern anatomical subdivision.
levator_caudae_brevis.location: Dorsal sacral/caudal vertebral region, close to the tail skeleton.
levator_caudae_brevis.attachments: Short connections between sacral/caudal vertebral processes; precise segment-to-segment attachments are not assigned from numbered slips.
levator_caudae_brevis.function: Elevate/extend the tail and contribute to local positioning; unilateral activity can produce lateral bending.
levator_caudae_brevis.nerve: Dorsal branches of caudal spinal nerves supply dorsal tail musculature.
levator_caudae_brevis.physio: Separate tail motion from spinal-cord level identification. A tail vertebra number does not name the supplying spinal segment.
levator_caudae_brevis.recall: How do short intervertebral connections differ mechanically from long tail tendons?

levator_caudae_longus.title: Long dorsal tail-muscle portions
levator_caudae_longus.overview: A functional source label for longer dorsal tail musculature, related to the dorsal sacrocaudal system.
levator_caudae_longus.location: Dorsal/lateral tail base and caudal continuation of epaxial tissues.
levator_caudae_longus.attachments: Lumbosacral/caudal vertebral process region to more distal caudal vertebrae through longer fascicles and tendons.
levator_caudae_longus.function: Extends/elevates the tail and assists directional control.
levator_caudae_longus.physio: Source boundaries should not be assumed to match every named sacrocaudal subdivision. Tail carriage reflects multiple muscles and behavioral state.
levator_caudae_longus.recall: Which longitudinal epaxial system continues toward the dorsal tail?

depressor_caudae_brevis.title: Short ventral tail-muscle portions
depressor_caudae_brevis.overview: Functional source labeling for short ventral tail flexor slips.
depressor_caudae_brevis.location: Ventral to the sacral/caudal skeleton, among other tail-base structures.
depressor_caudae_brevis.attachments: Short sacral/caudal intervertebral attachments; the mesh numbers do not verify exact anatomical levels.
depressor_caudae_brevis.function: Depress/flex the tail; asymmetric activity contributes to lateral tail positioning.
depressor_caudae_brevis.nerve: Ventral branches of caudal spinal nerves.
depressor_caudae_brevis.physio: Contrast ventral tail flexors with dorsal elevators, without interpreting posture alone as a neurologic finding.
depressor_caudae_brevis.recall: Which side of a tail vertebra does a depressor’s line of pull occupy?

coccygeus.title: Coccygeus
coccygeus.overview: A paired muscle forming part of the pelvic diaphragm and connecting pelvis to tail base.
coccygeus.location: Lateral pelvic outlet, adjacent to levator ani and caudal pelvic structures.
coccygeus.attachments: Ischiatic spine region to transverse processes of proximal caudal vertebrae.
coccygeus.function: Draws the tail ventrally/laterally and helps support the pelvic outlet.
coccygeus.physio: Its pelvic-diaphragm role is distinct from the thoracoabdominal diaphragm. The mesh is not a complete pelvic-floor assessment.
coccygeus.recall: What distinguishes coccygeus from the long dorsal tail muscles?

levator_ani.title: Levator ani
levator_ani.overview: A major paired skeletal-muscle component of the pelvic diaphragm.
levator_ani.location: Medial to coccygeus around the pelvic outlet, related to rectum and pelvic viscera.
levator_ani.attachments: Pelvic bony/fascial origins to caudal vertebral and perineal connective-tissue attachments through its subdivisions.
levator_ani.function: Supports pelvic viscera and controls pelvic-outlet/tail-base relationships.
levator_ani.nerve: Sacral somatic spinal branches; do not confuse these with autonomic pelvic-nerve functions.
levator_ani.physio: Pelvic support is a regional system involving fascia and other muscles, many of which are not separately represented here.
levator_ani.recall: Why is this called a pelvic diaphragm rather than a breathing muscle?

supraspinatus.title: Supraspinatus
supraspinatus.overview: An intrinsic shoulder muscle that links the scapula directly to the humerus. Its tendon is part of the shoulder's active support system.
supraspinatus.location: Occupies the fossa cranial to the scapular spine, deep to the superficial shoulder coverings.
supraspinatus.attachments: Supraspinous fossa and scapular spine to the greater tubercle of the humerus.
supraspinatus.function: Extends the shoulder and helps maintain alignment during loading. Its tendon crosses the cranial shoulder.
supraspinatus.physio: Relate shoulder support to both muscle activity and tendon integrity; a surface model cannot establish which tissue is painful.
supraspinatus.recall: Which scapular ridge separates this muscle from infraspinatus?

infraspinatus.title: Infraspinatus
infraspinatus.overview: A broad intrinsic shoulder muscle with an important lateral stabilizing role.
infraspinatus.location: Fills the infraspinous fossa, caudal to the scapular spine. Its tendon passes across the lateral shoulder.
infraspinatus.attachments: Infraspinous fossa to the lateral proximal humerus near the greater tubercle.
infraspinatus.function: Abducts and laterally rotates the humerus; its flexion or extension effect depends on joint position. Supports the shoulder laterally.
infraspinatus.physio: Compare muscle, tendon and joint position when studying shoulder mechanics; do not infer a fixed action from a single still pose.
infraspinatus.recall: Why can changing shoulder position change the tendon’s moment arm?

subscapularis.title: Subscapularis
subscapularis.overview: The principal muscle occupying the medial scapular surface.
subscapularis.location: Lies between the scapula and the thoracic wall; its short tendon crosses the medial shoulder capsule.
subscapularis.attachments: Subscapular fossa to the lesser tubercle of the humerus.
subscapularis.function: Adducts and stabilizes the arm, contributing to medial shoulder support and position-dependent shoulder motion.
subscapularis.nerve: Subscapular nerves; axillary contribution is described in canine regional anatomy.
subscapularis.physio: A lateral view hides much of this muscle. Rotate the model medially to understand how it opposes lateral shoulder displacement.
subscapularis.recall: Which humeral tubercle receives the tendon?

deltoideus_acromialis.title: Deltoideus · acromial part
deltoideus_acromialis.overview: One of the two canine deltoid parts, distinct from the scapular part.
deltoideus_acromialis.location: Superficial to the lateral shoulder, extending from the acromion toward the upper arm.
deltoideus_acromialis.attachments: Acromion to the deltoid tuberosity of the humerus.
deltoideus_acromialis.function: Flexes the shoulder and assists abduction of the humerus. It does not cross the elbow.
deltoideus_acromialis.physio: Compare its short acromial origin with the more extensive scapular origin of the other deltoid part.
deltoideus_acromialis.recall: Which joint can this part act on, and which adjacent joint can it not directly cross?

deltoideus_scapularis.title: Deltoideus · scapular part
deltoideus_scapularis.overview: The scapular portion of the deltoid muscle forms part of the superficial shoulder contour.
deltoideus_scapularis.location: Covers part of infraspinatus and converges toward the lateral humerus.
deltoideus_scapularis.attachments: Scapular spine through an aponeurotic attachment to the deltoid tuberosity.
deltoideus_scapularis.function: Flexes the shoulder and contributes to humeral abduction.
deltoideus_scapularis.physio: Study superficial deltoid separately from the deeper infraspinatus; their proximity does not make their actions identical.
deltoideus_scapularis.recall: What attachment is shared by the two deltoid parts?

teres_major.title: Teres major
teres_major.overview: A caudomedial shoulder muscle, often associated distally with the latissimus dorsi tendon.
teres_major.location: Runs from the caudal scapular angle to the medial proximal humerus, behind subscapularis.
teres_major.attachments: Caudal angle and adjacent border of scapula to the teres major tuberosity of the humerus.
teres_major.function: Flexes the shoulder, adducts the arm and contributes to medial rotation.
teres_major.physio: Its medial insertion explains why a purely lateral image can conceal its line of pull. Compare it with teres minor before memorizing actions.
teres_major.recall: How do the insertions of teres major and minor differ?

teres_minor.title: Teres minor
teres_minor.overview: A small intrinsic shoulder muscle adjacent to the lateral joint capsule.
teres_minor.location: Deep to the deltoid region, along the distal caudal scapula and caudolateral shoulder.
teres_minor.attachments: Distal caudal scapular border to the teres minor tuberosity of the humerus.
teres_minor.function: Flexes the shoulder and assists lateral rotation and local stabilization.
teres_minor.physio: Its small size makes isolation useful for learning relationships; small mesh size does not imply negligible stabilizing importance.
teres_minor.recall: Which larger muscle lies immediately cranial to its scapular region?

coracobrachialis.title: Coracobrachialis
coracobrachialis.overview: A short muscle spanning the medial shoulder.
coracobrachialis.location: Lies medial to the proximal humerus, close to the shoulder capsule and subscapularis tendon.
coracobrachialis.attachments: Coracoid process of the scapula to the medial humerus.
coracobrachialis.function: Adducts the arm and assists shoulder stabilization and extension.
coracobrachialis.physio: Distinguish this small medial shoulder muscle from brachialis, which primarily flexes the elbow.
coracobrachialis.recall: Does coracobrachialis attach to the radius or ulna?

biceps_brachii.title: Biceps brachii
biceps_brachii.overview: A two-joint muscle despite the single-headed canine proximal origin; its name should not be interpreted using human anatomy.
biceps_brachii.location: Runs along the cranial humerus; the proximal tendon passes through the intertubercular groove.
biceps_brachii.attachments: Supraglenoid tubercle of scapula to proximal radius and ulna.
biceps_brachii.function: Flexes the elbow and extends the shoulder; the proximal tendon also supports the shoulder.
biceps_brachii.physio: Consider both joints when reasoning about muscle length. Elbow motion alone does not describe the full length change of this muscle.
biceps_brachii.recall: Which two joint positions would lengthen its course? Explain anatomically rather than attempting a stretch.

brachialis.title: Brachialis
brachialis.overview: An elbow flexor with a curved course around the humerus.
brachialis.location: Occupies the brachialis groove, passing from the caudoproximal humerus toward the medial elbow.
brachialis.attachments: Proximal caudal humerus to the proximal medial ulna and radius.
brachialis.function: Flexes the elbow without crossing the shoulder.
brachialis.physio: Contrast this single-joint elbow flexor with biceps brachii. Their common distal region can obscure their different proximal relationships.
brachialis.recall: Why does shoulder position affect biceps length more directly than brachialis length?

triceps_brachii_long.title: Triceps brachii · long head
triceps_brachii_long.overview: The triceps head that spans both shoulder and elbow.
triceps_brachii_long.location: Forms much of the caudal arm between the scapula and olecranon.
triceps_brachii_long.attachments: Caudal border of scapula to olecranon through the common triceps tendon.
triceps_brachii_long.function: Extends the elbow and flexes the shoulder. Resists elbow collapse during weight bearing.
triceps_brachii_long.physio: Separate its two-joint behavior from the humeral triceps heads; all reach the olecranon, but only this head originates on the scapula.
triceps_brachii_long.recall: Which triceps head directly crosses the shoulder?

triceps_brachii_lateral.title: Triceps brachii · lateral head
triceps_brachii_lateral.overview: A humeral head of triceps visible on the lateral arm.
triceps_brachii_lateral.location: Lateral to the long head and proximal humerus, converging toward the elbow.
triceps_brachii_lateral.function: Extends the elbow; it does not directly move the shoulder because it does not cross that joint.
triceps_brachii_lateral.physio: When revising stance support, trace the triceps lever arm from the elbow axis to the olecranon.
triceps_brachii_lateral.recall: Why is the olecranon an important lever rather than just an attachment label?

triceps_brachii_medial.title: Triceps brachii · medial head
triceps_brachii_medial.overview: A smaller triceps head on the inner surface of the arm.
triceps_brachii_medial.location: Medial to the humerus, near the other elbow extensor components.
triceps_brachii_medial.function: Extends and stabilizes the elbow. Its direct mechanical effect is at the elbow, not the shoulder.
triceps_brachii_medial.physio: Medial access is needed to distinguish it from the long head and tensor fasciae antebrachii.
triceps_brachii_medial.recall: Which origin distinguishes this head from the long head?

triceps_brachii_accessory.title: Triceps brachii · accessory head
triceps_brachii_accessory.overview: The deep fourth head of the canine triceps complex.
triceps_brachii_accessory.location: Close to the caudal humerus and largely concealed by other triceps heads.
triceps_brachii_accessory.function: Contributes to elbow extension and active support of the elbow during loading.
triceps_brachii_accessory.physio: Isolate the deep portion to learn why the four anatomical heads may not be evident from the outer arm contour.
triceps_brachii_accessory.recall: Name the four canine triceps heads and identify the one arising on the scapula.

anconeus.title: Anconeus
anconeus.overview: A small elbow extensor closely related to the joint capsule.
anconeus.location: Caudal elbow, covering the olecranon fossa and proximal ulna.
anconeus.attachments: Distal humerus around the olecranon fossa to proximal lateral ulna.
anconeus.function: Assists elbow extension and draws the capsule away from the moving joint surfaces.
anconeus.physio: Its proximity to the capsule is useful for understanding joint mechanics; it cannot be assessed independently from a model image.
anconeus.recall: How does its position differ from the long head of triceps?

tensor_f.antebrachii.title: Tensor fasciae antebrachii
tensor_f.antebrachii.overview: A thin medial muscle that couples elbow extension with fascial tension.
tensor_f.antebrachii.location: Superficial on the medial triceps region, deep to surrounding trunk-to-limb structures.
tensor_f.antebrachii.attachments: Caudal scapular and latissimus-associated fascia to olecranon and antebrachial fascia.
tensor_f.antebrachii.function: Extends the elbow and tensions the forearm fascia.
tensor_f.antebrachii.physio: Distinguish the contractile muscle from the fascia it tensions; the model may not show the full continuous fascial sheet.
tensor_f.antebrachii.recall: Which connective tissue is named by this muscle?

extensor_capri_radialis.title: Extensor carpi radialis
extensor_capri_radialis.overview: A cranial forearm muscle with a name misspelled as capri in the source.
extensor_capri_radialis.location: The cranial margin of the antebrachium; tendon crosses the dorsal carpus.
extensor_capri_radialis.attachments: Lateral supracondylar region of humerus to dorsal bases of metacarpals II and III.
extensor_capri_radialis.function: Extends the carpus and helps maintain the paw’s supporting alignment.
extensor_capri_radialis.physio: Distinguish carpal extension from digital extension by following where the tendon stops.
extensor_capri_radialis.recall: Does this tendon continue to the distal phalanges?

extensor_capri_ulnaris.title: Ulnaris lateralis · extensor carpi ulnaris
extensor_capri_ulnaris.overview: A lateral forearm muscle whose traditional extensor name can mislead in the dog.
extensor_capri_ulnaris.location: Most lateral portion of the forearm extensor compartment, with tendons passing toward the lateral/palmar carpus.
extensor_capri_ulnaris.attachments: Lateral epicondyle of humerus to accessory carpal bone and proximal metacarpal V.
extensor_capri_ulnaris.function: Supports the loaded carpus and contributes to carpal flexion and paw abduction; do not treat it as a simple carpal extensor.
extensor_capri_ulnaris.nerve: Radial nerve, despite its supportive/flexor mechanical role.
extensor_capri_ulnaris.physio: This is a useful exception to learning muscle function solely from compartment or name.
extensor_capri_ulnaris.recall: Why is its nerve supply not enough to predict its exact action?

extensor_digitorum_communis.title: Common digital extensor · forelimb
extensor_digitorum_communis.overview: A multi-tendon extensor serving the main forepaw digits.
extensor_digitorum_communis.location: Craniolateral forearm; tendons traverse the dorsal carpus and metacarpus.
extensor_digitorum_communis.attachments: Lateral humeral epicondyle to extensor processes of distal phalanges II–V.
extensor_digitorum_communis.function: Extends the digits and assists carpal extension.
extensor_digitorum_communis.physio: Trace the tendon past the metacarpus to distinguish digital action from that of extensor carpi radialis.
extensor_digitorum_communis.recall: Which phalanx receives its terminal insertion?

extensor_digitorum_lat.title: Lateral digital extensor · forelimb
extensor_digitorum_lat.overview: A smaller digital extensor lateral to the common digital extensor.
extensor_digitorum_lat.location: Craniolateral antebrachium; its tendons join the extensor apparatus of the lateral digits.
extensor_digitorum_lat.attachments: Lateral humeral epicondylar region to the extensor tendons of digits III–V.
extensor_digitorum_lat.function: Extends the lateral digits and contributes to coordinated forepaw placement.
extensor_digitorum_lat.physio: The abbreviated source name is distinguished from the hindlimb lateral digital extensor using the model region.
extensor_digitorum_lat.recall: Which larger forelimb extensor lies next to it?

flexor_capri_radialis.title: Flexor carpi radialis
flexor_capri_radialis.overview: A medial carpal flexor; capri is a source spelling error.
flexor_capri_radialis.location: Superficial caudomedial forearm with a tendon on the medial/palmar carpus.
flexor_capri_radialis.attachments: Medial epicondyle of humerus to palmar proximal metacarpals II and III.
flexor_capri_radialis.function: Flexes the carpus and helps control it during limb loading.
flexor_capri_radialis.physio: Compare its palmar tendon course with the dorsal course of extensor carpi radialis.
flexor_capri_radialis.recall: How does tendon position relative to the carpus explain the opposite actions?

flexor_carpi_ulnaris.title: Flexor carpi ulnaris
flexor_carpi_ulnaris.overview: A two-headed carpal flexor on the caudal forearm.
flexor_carpi_ulnaris.location: Caudomedial antebrachium; humeral and ulnar portions converge distally.
flexor_carpi_ulnaris.attachments: Medial humeral epicondyle and olecranon to accessory carpal bone.
flexor_carpi_ulnaris.function: Flexes the carpus and contributes to lateral control of the paw.
flexor_carpi_ulnaris.physio: Identify the accessory carpal bone as a tendon attachment and lever; do not confuse it with the olecranon at the elbow.
flexor_carpi_ulnaris.recall: What are the two proximal origins?

flexor_digitorum_superficialis_fore.title: Superficial digital flexor · forelimb
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_fore.overview: A forepaw flexor whose tendons divide around the deeper digital-flexor tendons.
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_fore.location: Caudal antebrachium, superficial to much of the deep digital flexor; tendons continue down the palmar digits.
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_fore.attachments: Medial humeral epicondyle to middle phalanges of digits II–V.
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_fore.function: Flexes the digits, particularly through the proximal interphalangeal joints, and assists carpal flexion.
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_fore.physio: Differentiate a tendon ending at the middle phalanx from one reaching the distal phalanx.
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_fore.recall: Which deeper tendon passes through the superficial flexor’s split?

flexor_digitorum_profundus_fore.title: Deep digital flexor · forelimb
flexor_digitorum_profundus_fore.overview: A complex with humeral, radial and ulnar components whose tendons converge toward the paw.
flexor_digitorum_profundus_fore.location: Deep caudal forearm; the common tendon crosses the palmar carpus and divides to the digits.
flexor_digitorum_profundus_fore.attachments: Humerus, radius and ulna to flexor surfaces of the distal phalanges.
flexor_digitorum_profundus_fore.function: Flexes the digits including the distal interphalangeal joints and contributes to carpal flexion.
flexor_digitorum_profundus_fore.nerve: Median and ulnar nerves, with distribution varying between component heads.
flexor_digitorum_profundus_fore.physio: A rendered piece need not include all three heads. Use the source name only as a parent-muscle identification.
flexor_digitorum_profundus_fore.recall: How does its insertion level differ from the superficial digital flexor?

pronator_teres.title: Pronator teres
pronator_teres.overview: A short muscle crossing the medial elbow and proximal forearm.
pronator_teres.location: Oblique from the medial humeral epicondyle to the medial radius; near the median nerve.
pronator_teres.attachments: Medial humeral epicondyle to medial radial shaft.
pronator_teres.function: Pronates the forearm and can assist elbow flexion.
pronator_teres.physio: Canine forearm rotation is more restricted than the human pattern; do not transfer human range-of-motion values to this model.
pronator_teres.recall: Which bone rotates relative to its companion during pronation?

pronator_quadratus.title: Pronator quadratus
pronator_quadratus.overview: A deep pronator occupying the space between the forearm bones.
pronator_quadratus.location: Fills much of the interosseous interval between radius and ulna.
pronator_quadratus.attachments: Opposing surfaces of radius and ulna.
pronator_quadratus.function: Pronates and stabilizes the radius relative to the ulna.
pronator_quadratus.physio: The two-bone relationship is the key feature; the muscle does not extend from the trunk or across the shoulder.
pronator_quadratus.recall: Why is a medial or separated view helpful for finding it?

supinator.title: Supinator
supinator.overview: A short proximal forearm muscle that opposes pronation.
supinator.location: Craniolateral proximal radius, deep to superficial extensor muscles.
supinator.attachments: Lateral humeral epicondylar region to proximal cranial radius.
supinator.function: Supinates the forearm by rotating the radius laterally relative to the ulna.
supinator.physio: Study it with pronator teres and quadratus, without assuming human-like forearm mobility in the dog.
supinator.recall: Which nerve supplies this rotational muscle rather than the median nerve?

abductor_pollicis_longus.title: Abductor digiti I longus
abductor_pollicis_longus.overview: Also called abductor pollicis longus; a deep forearm muscle serving the medial first digit.
abductor_pollicis_longus.location: Its tendon crosses obliquely over the distal radius toward the medial carpus.
abductor_pollicis_longus.attachments: Lateral surfaces of radius and ulna and interosseous region to proximal metacarpal I.
abductor_pollicis_longus.function: Abducts digit I and contributes to carpal extension.
abductor_pollicis_longus.physio: Digit I is the dewclaw region, not one of the four principal ground-contact digits. Follow the tendon to establish this distinction.
abductor_pollicis_longus.recall: Why should pollicis not imply a human opposable thumb?

trapezius.title: Trapezius
trapezius.overview: A superficial extrinsic muscle with cervical and thoracic parts linking the scapula to the dorsal midline.
trapezius.location: Superficial neck and cranial thorax, over rhomboideus.
trapezius.attachments: Midline neck raphe and thoracic supraspinous region to scapular spine.
trapezius.function: Elevates and repositions the scapula; different fiber directions contribute to cranial or caudal scapular movement.
trapezius.nerve: Accessory nerve, with cervical sensory/proprioceptive contributions.
trapezius.physio: The scapula has muscular suspension rather than a bony articulation with the thorax; study this muscle as one contributor to that system.
trapezius.recall: What deeper muscle attaches to the dorsal scapular border?

rhomboideus.title: Rhomboideus
rhomboideus.overview: An extrinsic scapular muscle with head, cervical and thoracic portions.
rhomboideus.location: Deep to trapezius, along the dorsal scapular margin.
rhomboideus.attachments: Caudal head and dorsal cervical/thoracic midline regions to dorsal border of scapula.
rhomboideus.function: Elevates and stabilizes the scapula against the trunk and contributes to scapular repositioning.
rhomboideus.nerve: Ventral branches of cervical and thoracic spinal nerves.
rhomboideus.physio: Its dorsal attachment complements the ventral serratus sling. A grouped mesh may not separate all three anatomical portions.
rhomboideus.recall: How does its scapular insertion differ from that of trapezius?

latissimus_dors.title: Latissimus dorsi
latissimus_dors.overview: A broad extrinsic forelimb muscle connecting trunk fascia to the humerus.
latissimus_dors.location: Superficial dorsolateral thorax, narrowing toward the medial proximal arm.
latissimus_dors.attachments: Thoracolumbar fascia and associated caudal trunk attachments to the teres major region of the humerus.
latissimus_dors.function: Retracts the free limb and flexes the shoulder; with the limb fixed, it can draw the trunk forward.
latissimus_dors.physio: Distinguish open-chain limb movement from trunk movement over a weight-bearing limb. Neither is represented by the static pose alone.
latissimus_dors.recall: What changes when the distal limb is fixed?

omotransversarius.title: Omotransversarius
omotransversarius.overview: An extrinsic muscle linking the cranial neck to the scapula.
omotransversarius.location: A strap along the lateral neck, passing toward the acromion and distal scapular spine.
omotransversarius.attachments: Wing of atlas to acromion and distal scapular spine.
omotransversarius.function: Advances the scapular region when the neck is fixed; assists lateral neck bending when the limb is fixed.
omotransversarius.nerve: Accessory nerve and cervical spinal contributions.
omotransversarius.physio: Relate neck position to forelimb protraction during anatomical reasoning, without attributing every shortened stride to this one muscle.
omotransversarius.recall: Which cervical vertebra provides its cranial attachment?

brachiocephalicus.title: Brachiocephalicus
brachiocephalicus.overview: A composite extrinsic muscle divided at a clavicular intersection; the source groups its components.
brachiocephalicus.location: Superficial lateral neck and cranial arm, joining head/neck to humerus.
brachiocephalicus.attachments: Clavicular intersection connects cleidobrachialis at the humeral crest with cleidocephalicus portions toward the head and cervical raphe.
brachiocephalicus.function: Advances the free forelimb; with the limb fixed, head and neck position can change.
brachiocephalicus.nerve: Cleidobrachialis nerve for the arm portion; accessory and cervical contributions to the cranial portions.
brachiocephalicus.physio: Do not assign one undifferentiated nerve or origin to the whole grouped mesh. Learn the clavicular intersection as the organizing landmark.
brachiocephalicus.recall: Which component lies distal to the clavicular intersection?

thoracis_serratus_ventr.title: Serratus ventralis
thoracis_serratus_ventr.overview: The major muscular sling suspending the trunk between the forelimbs.
thoracis_serratus_ventr.location: Deep between scapula and lateral neck/thorax; cervical and thoracic fibers converge on the medial scapula.
thoracis_serratus_ventr.attachments: Cervical transverse processes and cranial ribs to the serrated face of scapula.
thoracis_serratus_ventr.function: Supports the trunk and controls scapular translation and rotation. Different regions have different lines of pull.
thoracis_serratus_ventr.nerve: Cervical spinal branches to the cervical part; long thoracic nerve to the thoracic part.
thoracis_serratus_ventr.physio: Think of load transfer through a muscular sling, not a human-style clavicular shoulder girdle.
thoracis_serratus_ventr.recall: What would a lateral skeleton-only view omit about trunk support?

thoracis_m_pectoralis_profundus.title: Deep pectoral muscle
thoracis_m_pectoralis_profundus.overview: A broad ventral extrinsic muscle connecting the sternum to the proximal humerus.
thoracis_m_pectoralis_profundus.location: Deep to the superficial pectorals, along the ventral thorax and medial shoulder.
thoracis_m_pectoralis_profundus.attachments: Sternum and adjacent ventral thoracic connective tissues to proximal humerus, chiefly near the lesser tubercle.
thoracis_m_pectoralis_profundus.function: Adducts and retracts the free limb; helps draw the trunk over a fixed limb and supports limb-to-trunk stability.
thoracis_m_pectoralis_profundus.physio: Its action depends on whether the limb is bearing weight. The axillary region also contains major vessels and nerves.
thoracis_m_pectoralis_profundus.recall: Why does a fixed-paw task change the structure that moves?

pectorales_superficiales.title: Superficial pectoral muscles
pectorales_superficiales.overview: Descending and transverse portions form the superficial ventral connection to the forelimb. Source numbers do not reliably identify each portion.
pectorales_superficiales.location: Cranial ventral thorax, superficial to deep pectoral and medial to the upper forelimb.
pectorales_superficiales.attachments: Cranial sternum to humeral crest and adjacent arm/forearm fascia, according to portion.
pectorales_superficiales.function: Adduct the forelimb and limit excessive abduction during support.
pectorales_superficiales.physio: Learn the superficial versus deep pectoral planes before assigning individual mesh numbers to named parts.
pectorales_superficiales.recall: Which pectoral group is innervated by the cranial pectoral nerves?

temporalis.title: Temporalis
temporalis.overview: A major jaw-closing muscle occupying much of the lateral/dorsal skull in the dog.
temporalis.location: Temporal fossa, deep to temporal fascia and superficial to the cranial vault.
temporalis.attachments: Temporal fossa and temporal fascia to coronoid process of mandible.
temporalis.function: Elevates the mandible, closing the jaw; fiber direction also helps control mandibular position.
temporalis.nerve: Deep temporal branches of the mandibular division of trigeminal nerve (CN V).
temporalis.physio: Distinguish muscles of mastication from facial-expression muscles. Their motor nerve supply differs.

masseter.title: Masseter
masseter.overview: A powerful layered muscle for jaw closure.
masseter.location: Lateral to the mandibular ramus, below the zygomatic arch.
masseter.attachments: Zygomatic arch to masseteric fossa and lateral mandibular ramus.
masseter.function: Elevates the mandible and contributes to stable occlusion during chewing.
masseter.nerve: Masseteric branch of mandibular division of trigeminal nerve (CN V).
masseter.physio: A single external mesh may combine deeper and superficial layers. Muscle contour alone does not establish bite force or discomfort.
masseter.recall: What bony arch forms its major cranial attachment?

pterygoideus_med.title: Medial pterygoid
pterygoideus_med.overview: A deep jaw-closing muscle on the inner side of the mandibular ramus.
pterygoideus_med.location: Medial to the mandible, near the pterygoid region of the skull.
pterygoideus_med.attachments: Pterygoid/palatine/sphenoid region to medial mandibular ramus.
pterygoideus_med.function: Elevates the mandible and assists small transverse movements during chewing.
pterygoideus_med.nerve: Mandibular division of trigeminal nerve (CN V).
pterygoideus_med.physio: Compare its medial location with the lateral masseter; together they provide complementary support around the mandibular ramus.
pterygoideus_med.recall: Which similarly named muscle lies closer to the mandibular condyle?

pterygoideus_lat.title: Lateral pterygoid
pterygoideus_lat.overview: A smaller deep masticatory muscle near the temporomandibular joint.
pterygoideus_lat.location: Medial to the mandibular condylar region, dorsal to much of the medial pterygoid.
pterygoideus_lat.attachments: Sphenoid/pterygoid region to medial mandibular condylar neck and associated joint tissues.
pterygoideus_lat.function: Contributes to protraction and small side-to-side mandibular positioning.
pterygoideus_lat.nerve: Mandibular division of trigeminal nerve (CN V).
pterygoideus_lat.physio: Canine jaw mechanics are mainly hinge-like compared with species specialized for grinding; do not import large human or herbivore excursions.
pterygoideus_lat.recall: How does its condylar attachment differ from temporalis’s coronoid attachment?

digastricus.title: Digastricus
digastricus.overview: The principal jaw opener, with rostral and caudal portions that can appear continuous in the dog.
digastricus.location: Ventral/caudal to the mandible, extending from the caudal skull toward the jaw body.
digastricus.attachments: Jugular process of occipital bone to ventral/medial mandible.
digastricus.function: Depresses the mandible and opens the mouth when the cranial attachment is stabilized.
digastricus.nerve: Rostral portion: mandibular division of CN V; caudal portion: facial nerve (CN VII).
digastricus.physio: Its dual motor supply is a useful contrast with the jaw-closing muscles. Do not interpret one grouped mesh as one nerve territory.
digastricus.recall: Which cranial nerve supplies the caudal portion?

mylohyoideus.title: Mylohyoideus
mylohyoideus.overview: A thin muscular floor supporting the tongue and oral cavity.
mylohyoideus.location: Between the medial surfaces of the mandibles, ventral to the tongue.
mylohyoideus.attachments: Mylohyoid lines of mandibles to a median raphe and basihyoid region.
mylohyoideus.function: Elevates/supports the oral floor and tongue during swallowing-related movement.
mylohyoideus.nerve: Mylohyoid branch of mandibular division of trigeminal nerve (CN V).
mylohyoideus.physio: It is a floor-of-mouth structure, not a primary cervical postural muscle. Nearby tongue and hyoid structures may not all be modeled.
mylohyoideus.recall: What midline structure joins its left and right sheets?

geniohyoideus.title: Geniohyoideus
geniohyoideus.overview: A paired strap muscle connecting the rostral mandible to the hyoid.
geniohyoideus.location: Deep to mylohyoideus, along the ventral oral floor.
geniohyoideus.attachments: Mandibular symphyseal region to basihyoid bone.
geniohyoideus.function: Draws the hyoid and tongue base rostrally during coordinated oral/swallowing movements.
geniohyoideus.physio: Distinguish movement of the hyoid from movement of the mandible. Muscle action depends on which attachment is stabilized.
geniohyoideus.recall: Which bone forms its caudal attachment?

buccinator.title: Buccinator
buccinator.overview: A cheek muscle that keeps food between the teeth; it belongs to facial musculature rather than the jaw-closing group.
buccinator.location: Within the cheek wall, lateral to the oral cavity and deep to superficial facial tissues.
buccinator.attachments: Maxillary/mandibular alveolar regions to the cheek and mouth-angle muscular complex.
buccinator.function: Compresses the cheek against the teeth and assists food handling.
buccinator.physio: The buccal nerve of CN V is sensory, whereas facial-nerve branches provide the muscle’s motor control. Do not confuse the similarly named nerves.
buccinator.recall: Why is buccinator not grouped with masseter for motor innervation?

orbicularis_oris.title: Orbicularis oris
orbicularis_oris.overview: A lip-associated sphincter-like muscle integrated with neighboring facial muscles.
orbicularis_oris.location: Within upper and lower lips around the oral opening.
orbicularis_oris.attachments: Fibers interlace around the mouth and with adjacent facial-muscle insertions rather than forming one simple bone-to-bone span.
orbicularis_oris.function: Closes and shapes the lips during feeding and facial movement.
orbicularis_oris.physio: Lip motor control differs from jaw force. An outer face model does not show all layered insertions or mucosal relationships.
orbicularis_oris.recall: Which nerve closes the lips, and which nerve primarily closes the jaw?

orbicularis_oculi.title: Orbicularis oculi
orbicularis_oculi.overview: The eyelid-closing facial muscle surrounding the palpebral opening.
orbicularis_oculi.location: Within and around the eyelids, superficial to the orbit.
orbicularis_oculi.attachments: Medial orbital/palpebral attachments and interlacing eyelid fibers.
orbicularis_oculi.function: Closes the eyelids for blinking and protective eye coverage.
orbicularis_oculi.nerve: Facial nerve (CN VII); sensory input for corneal reflexes uses trigeminal pathways, not the same motor nerve.
orbicularis_oculi.physio: Separate eyelid motion from movement of the eyeball. The atlas does not reproduce the full protective reflex circuit.
orbicularis_oculi.recall: Which cranial nerve provides the motor limb of eyelid closure?

retractor_anguli_oculi.title: Retractor anguli oculi lateralis
retractor_anguli_oculi.overview: A small facial muscle acting on the lateral eyelid angle.
retractor_anguli_oculi.location: Lateral to the palpebral opening, near temporal/zygomatic fascia.
retractor_anguli_oculi.attachments: Temporal/zygomatic fascial region to lateral angle of the eyelids.
retractor_anguli_oculi.function: Retracts the lateral eyelid angle, modifying the palpebral opening.
retractor_anguli_oculi.physio: Do not confuse it with retractor bulbi, which retracts the eyeball and has a different innervation.
retractor_anguli_oculi.recall: Which structure does this muscle move: eyelid angle or globe?

levator_labii_sup.title: Levator labii superioris
levator_labii_sup.overview: A facial muscle elevating the upper lip.
levator_labii_sup.location: Rostral face, extending from the infraorbital/maxillary region into the upper lip.
levator_labii_sup.attachments: Maxillary region to upper lip through facial soft-tissue attachments.
levator_labii_sup.function: Raises the upper lip and helps alter the oral opening.
levator_labii_sup.physio: The nearby infraorbital nerve is chiefly sensory to the region; proximity is not proof that it supplies this muscle’s motor action.
levator_labii_sup.recall: Which nerve division carries facial sensation near the upper lip?

caninus.title: Caninus
caninus.overview: A facial muscle associated with the upper lip and nasal region.
caninus.location: Lateral rostral face, close to other upper-lip and nasal facial muscles.
caninus.attachments: Maxillary region to upper-lip/nasal soft tissues.
caninus.function: Elevates/retracts upper-lip tissues and contributes to shaping the rostral facial opening.
caninus.physio: Its name is shared with a tooth type; do not confuse the muscle with the canine tooth or a jaw-closing muscle.
caninus.recall: Does its motor supply follow facial-expression or mastication pathways?

zygomaticus.title: Zygomaticus
zygomaticus.overview: A slender facial muscle drawing the mouth angle caudally.
zygomaticus.location: Superficial lateral face, extending toward the oral commissure.
zygomaticus.attachments: Scutiform/adjacent auricular fascial region to angle of the mouth.
zygomaticus.function: Retracts the oral commissure and participates in facial expression and food handling.
zygomaticus.physio: Facial movements involve several interlacing muscles; a single mesh is not an independent measure of facial-nerve function.
zygomaticus.recall: What is the anatomical term for the mouth corner?

interscutularis.title: Interscutularis
interscutularis.overview: An auricular-associated facial muscle linking the scutiform-cartilage regions across the head.
interscutularis.location: Superficial dorsal head between the bases of the external ears.
interscutularis.attachments: Left and right scutiform-cartilage/fascial regions through the intervening muscular sheet.
interscutularis.function: Repositions the scutiform cartilages and assists coordinated ear positioning.
interscutularis.physio: Ear orientation is not a measure of spinal mobility. Distinguish auricular muscles from the much deeper temporalis beneath them.
interscutularis.recall: Which cartilage helps organize the small external-ear muscles?

Skutulum.title: Scutiform cartilage · likely source identity
Skutulum.overview: The nonstandard label and head location suggest the small scutiform cartilage, an attachment platform for auricular muscles.
Skutulum.location: Superficial head near the medial/rostral base of the external ear.
Skutulum.attachments: Cartilaginous support embedded in auricular connective tissue with multiple small muscle attachments; it is not a freely articulated skull bone.
Skutulum.function: Transmits forces between auricular muscles during external-ear positioning.
Skutulum.nerve: Cartilage has no skeletal-muscle motor innervation; surrounding auricular muscles are supplied by CN VII.
Skutulum.physio: Keep the probable identity qualification visible. A source prefix m_ does not prove that a piece is contractile muscle.
Skutulum.recall: Why should this source item be treated as connective/supporting tissue?

eye.title: Eye / globe surface
eye.overview: The selected eye piece is a surface representation of the ocular region, not a full eye dissection. Multiple source pieces can overlap here.
eye.location: Within the orbit, deep to the eyelids and adjacent to extraocular muscles and orbital tissues.
eye.attachments: The globe is supported by orbital connective tissue and moved by extraocular muscle insertions; lens, retina and internal layers are not separately identified here.
eye.function: Vision and gaze orientation contribute to navigation and postural control, but these functions are not simulated by this mesh.
eye.nerve: Optic nerve carries visual input; CN III, IV and VI control extraocular muscles.
eye.physio: Distinguish a visual model from a clinical vision or vestibular examination. The selected piece alone does not encode all those pathways.
eye.recall: Which cranial nerve carries visual information rather than moving the globe?

nose.title: External nose surface
nose.overview: A representation of the external nasal region rather than the internal nasal cavity.
nose.location: Rostral muzzle, surrounding the external nares.
nose.attachments: Nasal skin/planum and underlying cartilage/soft-tissue support connect with surrounding muzzle structures.
nose.function: Provides the external entrance for airflow and odor sampling; nostril shaping depends on adjacent facial muscles.
nose.nerve: Regional sensation is mainly trigeminal; adjacent facial muscles use CN VII. Olfactory pathways are internal and not displayed.
nose.physio: Do not label this external surface as the olfactory nerve or nasal turbinates. Study the difference between a visible opening and deeper sensory anatomy.
nose.recall: What important nasal structures are absent from an outer surface mesh?

skin.title: Body surface
skin.overview: A whole-body outer surface used for orientation, not a layered histological skin model.
skin.location: Covers the musculoskeletal structures and provides the external body contour.
skin.attachments: Epidermis, dermis and subcutaneous attachments relate skin to underlying fascia; regional mobility and thickness vary.
skin.function: Protection, sensation and a mechanical interface with the environment. The mesh does not encode coat, tissue compliance or temperature.
skin.nerve: Regional cutaneous nerves supply sensation; sympathetic fibers serve vessels and skin appendages.
skin.physio: Use it to relate deeper anatomy to body landmarks. Do not infer tissue glide, pain or treatment dosage from surface geometry.
skin.recall: How would removing the outer layer change your understanding of a palpable landmark?

Ligament.title: Unspecified ligament · identity unresolved
Ligament.overview: The source names this piece only Ligament. Its dorsal cervicothoracic location suggests a supporting structure, but no exact ligament identity is asserted.
Ligament.location: Near the dorsal neck/cranial thoracic region in the reference pose.
Ligament.attachments: Ligaments generally connect skeletal elements and blend with periosteal/capsular tissues; the two ends of this particular mesh are not anatomically verified.
Ligament.function: Passive collagenous structures constrain or guide movement and can contain mechanosensory endings; precise function depends on the actual ligament.
Ligament.nerve: No motor supply; sensory innervation depends on the verified local ligament.
Ligament.physio: Do not use this ambiguous mesh to memorize a nuchal- or supraspinous-ligament attachment or to plan an intervention.
Ligament.recall: What two confirmed attachments would be needed before assigning a name?

abdominis_Aponeurosis.title: Abdominal aponeurosis
abdominis_Aponeurosis.overview: A source representation of sheet-like abdominal connective tissue; the exact contributing layers are not individually resolved.
abdominis_Aponeurosis.location: Ventral/lateral abdominal wall, continuous with broad muscle attachments.
abdominis_Aponeurosis.attachments: Aponeuroses of broad abdominal muscles contribute to the rectus sheath and linea alba. This mesh should not be assumed to contain every layer.
abdominis_Aponeurosis.function: Transmits muscle force and distributes tension across the abdominal wall. It does not actively contract.
abdominis_Aponeurosis.nerve: Sensory nerve endings may occur in connective tissue; no skeletal-muscle motor innervation.
abdominis_Aponeurosis.physio: Differentiate muscle, aponeurosis and linea alba when learning abdominal support. A fascial sheet is not simply an inactive muscle belly.
abdominis_Aponeurosis.recall: Which midline structure receives contributions from both sides of the abdominal wall?

dorsi_Fascia_thoracolumbar.title: Thoracolumbar fascia
dorsi_Fascia_thoracolumbar.overview: A strong regional connective-tissue sheet associated with epaxial and abdominal attachments.
dorsi_Fascia_thoracolumbar.location: Over the dorsal/lateral thoracolumbar musculature, continuous with neighboring fascia.
dorsi_Fascia_thoracolumbar.attachments: Vertebral and pelvic attachments link with aponeurotic contributions from surrounding trunk muscles. The surface model does not separate all fascial layers.
dorsi_Fascia_thoracolumbar.function: Distributes tensile forces and provides muscle attachment/support; it is not a contractile spinal extensor.
dorsi_Fascia_thoracolumbar.nerve: Regional sensory innervation; no motor nerve in the sense used for skeletal muscle.
dorsi_Fascia_thoracolumbar.physio: Avoid converting a visible fascial continuity into an unverified claim about a treatment pathway. Study the actual neighboring attachments first.
dorsi_Fascia_thoracolumbar.recall: Which epaxial muscle lies deep to this sheet in the lumbar region?

biceps_femoris_tendon.title: Biceps femoris · tendon/aponeurotic portion
biceps_femoris_tendon.overview: A noncontractile source piece associated with the broad distal attachments of biceps femoris.
biceps_femoris_tendon.location: Distal lateral thigh/crural fascial region, continuous with the muscle’s force-transmitting tissues.
biceps_femoris_tendon.attachments: Biceps femoris connects distally with patellar/tibial fascia and the common calcanean pathway; this piece may represent only part of that complex.
biceps_femoris_tendon.function: Transmits force generated by biceps femoris across its distal connections. It does not generate force through contraction itself.
biceps_femoris_tendon.nerve: Tendinous sensory endings; the parent muscle’s motor supply is through sciatic-associated branches.
biceps_femoris_tendon.physio: Keep parent-muscle actions separate from the properties of a tendon. Exact strain or tissue health cannot be inferred from the model.
biceps_femoris_tendon.recall: Why can a tendon piece share a muscle’s name without sharing its tissue type?

gluteus_superficialis_major.title: Superficial gluteal muscle
gluteus_superficialis_major.overview: A superficial hip muscle; major in the model name is not a separate canine gluteal designation.
gluteus_superficialis_major.location: Lateral pelvis, superficial to the middle gluteal and cranial to much of biceps femoris.
gluteus_superficialis_major.attachments: Sacral/first caudal region and sacrotuberous ligament to the third trochanter of the femur.
gluteus_superficialis_major.function: Extends and abducts the hip, contributing to lateral pelvic-limb control.
gluteus_superficialis_major.physio: Distinguish this muscle from the much larger middle gluteal and avoid translating its source label into human gluteus maximus anatomy.
gluteus_superficialis_major.recall: Which femoral prominence receives the superficial gluteal insertion?

gluteus_medius.title: Middle gluteal muscle
gluteus_medius.overview: A substantial hip extensor over the lateral ilium.
gluteus_medius.location: Deep to superficial gluteal coverings and superficial to the deep gluteal region.
gluteus_medius.attachments: Gluteal surface and crest of ilium to greater trochanter of femur.
gluteus_medius.function: Extends and abducts the hip; helps control the pelvis over the supporting limb.
gluteus_medius.physio: Relate its attachment to propulsion and pelvic stability; visible muscle bulk is not a direct measure of strength or activation.
gluteus_medius.recall: How does its insertion differ from that of superficial gluteal?

gluteus_profundus_minor.title: Deep gluteal muscle
gluteus_profundus_minor.overview: The deepest gluteal muscle; minor is retained only as source wording.
gluteus_profundus_minor.location: Immediately lateral to the hip capsule, beneath middle gluteal.
gluteus_profundus_minor.attachments: Lateral body of ilium and adjacent ischiatic spine region to greater trochanter.
gluteus_profundus_minor.function: Abducts the hip and contributes to medial rotation and joint stabilization.
gluteus_profundus_minor.physio: Rotate to the deep lateral hip to distinguish it from short lateral rotators caudal to the joint.
gluteus_profundus_minor.recall: Which short hip muscles lie caudal to this muscle?

biceps_femoris.title: Biceps femoris
biceps_femoris.overview: A large lateral hamstring with several functional portions and broad distal fascial connections.
biceps_femoris.location: Superficial lateral and caudal thigh, covering deeper hamstrings and much of the sciatic nerve course.
biceps_femoris.attachments: Ischiatic tuberosity and sacrotuberous ligament to patellar/tibial regions through fascia, with a contribution toward the calcaneal tendon.
biceps_femoris.function: Extends the hip. Cranial and caudal portions can respectively extend and flex the stifle; distal connections assist tarsal extension.
biceps_femoris.nerve: Primarily sciatic nerve branches; the cranial portion may also receive a caudal gluteal contribution.
biceps_femoris.physio: Do not assign one stifle action to every fiber. Study each portion relative to the stifle axis.
biceps_femoris.recall: Why can one named muscle have opposing stifle actions?

semitendinosus.title: Semitendinosus
semitendinosus.overview: A caudal hamstring spanning the hip and stifle, with a distal calcaneal contribution.
semitendinosus.location: Forms a recognizable caudal thigh contour beside semimembranosus and biceps femoris.
semitendinosus.attachments: Ischiatic tuberosity to proximal medial tibia and calcaneal tuber through a tendinous contribution.
semitendinosus.function: Extends the hip, flexes the stifle and contributes to tarsal extension.
semitendinosus.nerve: Sciatic nerve, principally its tibial component.
semitendinosus.physio: Consider the entire multi-joint course when studying muscle length or stance-to-swing transitions.
semitendinosus.recall: Which distal attachment allows an influence beyond the stifle?

semimembranosus.title: Semimembranosus
semimembranosus.overview: A broad medial hamstring with separate femoral and tibial insertions.
semimembranosus.location: Caudomedial thigh, deep/medial to semitendinosus and biceps femoris.
semimembranosus.attachments: Ischiatic tuberosity to medial distal femur and proximal medial tibia through distinct parts.
semimembranosus.function: Extends the hip and adducts the limb; the tibial portion can flex the stifle, while the femoral portion does not cross it.
semimembranosus.physio: Distinguish anatomical parts before describing stifle effects. A grouped surface may combine both insertions.
semimembranosus.recall: Which portion directly crosses the stifle?

sartorius.title: Sartorius · cranial and caudal parts
sartorius.overview: In dogs, two strap-like portions cross the cranial/medial thigh; source suffixes do not confirm which is selected.
sartorius.location: Cranial and medial thigh, superficial to quadriceps and adjacent to the femoral triangle.
sartorius.attachments: Iliac crest/ventral iliac region to patella through the cranial part and proximal medial tibia through the caudal part.
sartorius.function: Both flex the hip; the cranial part extends the stifle and the caudal part flexes it.
sartorius.physio: Keep the opposite stifle actions separate. These notes describe both parts when the model identification is incomplete.
sartorius.recall: What distal attachment explains each part’s stifle action?

gracilis.title: Gracilis
gracilis.overview: A broad superficial medial thigh muscle with extensive fascial and tendinous attachments.
gracilis.location: Medial thigh, covering portions of the adductor group.
gracilis.attachments: Pelvic symphysial region through the symphysial tendon to tibial/crural fascia and a calcaneal contribution.
gracilis.function: Adducts the limb; contributes to stifle flexion and tarsal extension through its distal connections.
gracilis.physio: Distinguish medial limb stabilization from forward propulsion; adductors help control limb position as load changes.
gracilis.recall: Which nerve chiefly supplies the medial thigh adductor group?

pectineus.title: Pectineus
pectineus.overview: A relatively small proximal medial thigh adductor.
pectineus.location: Between sartorius and the deeper adductor region, near the femoral triangle.
pectineus.attachments: Pecten of pubis and iliopubic eminence region to the medial femoral shaft.
pectineus.function: Adducts the hip and contributes to control of proximal limb position.
pectineus.physio: Its deep medial location is close to important vessels and nerves; use the model for orientation, not blind palpation or treatment placement.
pectineus.recall: Does its femoral insertion allow it to cross the stifle?

adductor_magnus.title: Adductor · magnus/brevis region
adductor_magnus.overview: A deep medial thigh adductor complex; canine subdivisions may be less sharply separable than a source name suggests.
adductor_magnus.location: Deep to gracilis, extending from the ventral pelvis to the caudomedial femur.
adductor_magnus.attachments: Pubic/ischiatic symphysial region to the caudal femoral shaft.
adductor_magnus.function: Adducts the hip and assists hip extension and stance stabilization.
adductor_magnus.physio: A mesh boundary is not proof of a complete anatomical fascial boundary. Compare this region with pectineus and adductor longus.
adductor_magnus.recall: Which attachment prevents a direct action across the tarsus?

adductor_longus.title: Adductor longus
adductor_longus.overview: A small medial thigh adductor, variably distinct from adjacent adductor tissue.
adductor_longus.location: Proximomedial thigh near pectineus and the larger adductor mass.
adductor_longus.function: Adducts the limb and contributes to hip stabilization.
adductor_longus.physio: Treat its distinctness as anatomical/model variation; compare it with the larger source-labeled adductor magnus portion.
adductor_longus.recall: Which muscle group shares its motor nerve?

abductor_cruris.title: Caudal crural abductor
abductor_cruris.overview: A thin accessory muscle associated with the caudal thigh.
abductor_cruris.location: Deep to biceps femoris, extending toward the lateral fascia of the crus.
abductor_cruris.attachments: Sacrotuberous ligament region to crural fascia.
abductor_cruris.function: Helps abduct the limb and tension the lateral crural fascia.
abductor_cruris.physio: Separate this small muscle from biceps femoris rather than assuming all lateral thigh tissue belongs to the hamstrings.
abductor_cruris.recall: Why does the name crural refer to the distal fascial connection?

rectus_femoris.title: Rectus femoris
rectus_femoris.overview: The quadriceps component that crosses both hip and stifle.
rectus_femoris.location: Cranial thigh, superficial to vastus intermedius and between the other vasti.
rectus_femoris.attachments: Ilium cranial to acetabulum to patella through quadriceps tendon, then tibial tuberosity through patellar ligament.
rectus_femoris.function: Extends the stifle and flexes the hip.
rectus_femoris.physio: Hip position changes its length directly; the other three quadriceps heads originate on the femur and do not cross the hip.
rectus_femoris.recall: Which quadriceps head has an iliac origin?

vastus_lat.title: Vastus lateralis
vastus_lat.overview: The lateral femoral head of the quadriceps group.
vastus_lat.location: Craniolateral thigh, adjacent to rectus femoris and lateral to vastus intermedius.
vastus_lat.attachments: Proximal/lateral femoral shaft to patella and indirectly tibial tuberosity through the extensor apparatus.
vastus_lat.function: Extends the stifle and contributes to active support during weight bearing.
vastus_lat.physio: Compare the patellar tendon pathway with that of rectus femoris while keeping their different proximal origins clear.
vastus_lat.recall: Does this head directly flex the hip?

vastus_med.title: Vastus medialis
vastus_med.overview: The medial femoral head of quadriceps.
