vastus_med.location: Craniomedial thigh, adjacent to the patella and medial femur.
vastus_med.attachments: Proximal/medial femoral shaft to patella through quadriceps tendon.
vastus_med.function: Extends the stifle and helps coordinate the patellar extensor mechanism.
vastus_med.physio: Avoid importing human-specific claims about isolated vastus-medialis training into canine anatomy. Learn the canine attachments and group function first.
vastus_med.recall: Which ligament transmits quadriceps force from patella to tibia?

vastus_intermedius.title: Vastus intermedius
vastus_intermedius.overview: The deepest quadriceps head, lying directly on the cranial femur.
vastus_intermedius.location: Deep to rectus femoris and between medial and lateral vasti.
vastus_intermedius.attachments: Cranial/lateral femoral shaft to patella through quadriceps tendon.
vastus_intermedius.function: Extends the stifle without directly crossing the hip.
vastus_intermedius.physio: Hiding the superficial quadriceps pieces reveals its relation to the femoral shaft.
vastus_intermedius.recall: Why is this head not well represented by the superficial thigh outline?

tensor_f.latae.title: Tensor fasciae latae
tensor_f.latae.overview: A proximal thigh muscle whose insertion is largely fascial.
tensor_f.latae.location: Craniolateral hip and thigh, superficial to the cranial quadriceps region.
tensor_f.latae.attachments: Tuber coxae and adjacent iliac/gluteal fascia to fascia lata, which blends with the stifle extensor apparatus.
tensor_f.latae.function: Tenses fascia lata, flexes the hip and assists stifle extension through fascial connections.
tensor_f.latae.physio: A muscle can influence a joint through fascia rather than a narrow terminal tendon. Trace the fascial continuation instead of stopping at the muscle belly.
tensor_f.latae.recall: What tissue connects this muscle to the stifle region?

iliacus.title: Iliacus
iliacus.overview: One of the components that join to form iliopsoas.
iliacus.location: Medial surface of ilium, deep in the proximal pelvic limb.
iliacus.attachments: Iliac fossa/medial iliac region to lesser trochanter via the common iliopsoas insertion.
iliacus.function: Flexes the hip and helps position the femur relative to the pelvis.
iliacus.physio: The model separates iliacus and psoas major; learn their common distal attachment and different proximal origins.
iliacus.recall: Which muscle joins iliacus before insertion?

psoas_major.title: Psoas major
psoas_major.overview: The lumbar component of iliopsoas, connecting the axial skeleton to the proximal femur.
psoas_major.location: Ventral to lumbar vertebrae, extending through the deep pelvic region toward the hip.
psoas_major.attachments: Lumbar vertebral bodies and transverse processes to lesser trochanter with iliacus.
psoas_major.function: Flexes the hip; with the limb fixed, contributes to lumbar/pelvic positioning.
psoas_major.nerve: Lumbar ventral spinal branches and femoral nerve contributions.
psoas_major.physio: Its two-region connection makes pelvic and lumbar position relevant to its length; a visible surface alone cannot identify an iliopsoas injury.
psoas_major.recall: Which femoral trochanter is the iliopsoas insertion?

psoas_minor.title: Psoas minor
psoas_minor.overview: A hypaxial muscle that ends on the pelvis rather than crossing the hip to the femur.
psoas_minor.location: Ventral lumbar region, associated with but distinct from psoas major.
psoas_minor.attachments: Caudal thoracic/lumbar vertebral bodies to the arcuate-line/iliopubic region of the ilium.
psoas_minor.function: Flexes and stabilizes the lumbar spine and can influence pelvic position.
psoas_minor.nerve: Ventral branches of lumbar spinal nerves.
psoas_minor.physio: Do not automatically give it the hip-flexor action of iliopsoas; check its pelvic insertion.
psoas_minor.recall: Which psoas muscle does not insert on the lesser trochanter?

obturatorius_int.title: Internal obturator
obturatorius_int.overview: A deep hip muscle with a tendon that changes direction at the pelvis.
obturatorius_int.location: On the pelvic surface around the obturator foramen; tendon exits toward the trochanteric fossa.
obturatorius_int.attachments: Internal surface of the obturator membrane and adjacent pelvic bone to trochanteric fossa of femur.
obturatorius_int.function: Laterally rotates the hip and contributes to deep joint stabilization.
obturatorius_int.physio: Follow the bent tendon course rather than drawing a straight line through the pelvis when reasoning about its action.
obturatorius_int.recall: Where does the tendon leave the pelvic surface?

obturatorius_ext.title: External obturator
obturatorius_ext.overview: A deep medial hip muscle distinct from the internal obturator despite a shared distal region.
obturatorius_ext.location: External/ventral aspect of the obturator membrane, deep to medial thigh muscles.
obturatorius_ext.attachments: External obturator membrane and surrounding pubis/ischium to trochanteric fossa.
obturatorius_ext.function: Laterally rotates and stabilizes the hip.
obturatorius_ext.physio: The internal and external obturators differ in nerve supply and route to the femur.
obturatorius_ext.recall: Which obturator is supplied by the obturator nerve?

gemellus.title: Gemelli
gemellus.overview: Short deep muscles associated with the internal obturator tendon.
gemellus.location: Caudal to the hip capsule, flanking the internal obturator tendon near the lesser ischiatic notch.
gemellus.attachments: Ischiatic region to trochanteric fossa, in association with the internal obturator insertion.
gemellus.function: Laterally rotate and help stabilize the hip.
gemellus.physio: A single named mesh may combine the paired slips. Use the tendon between them as an identification landmark.
gemellus.recall: What tendon gives the gemelli their paired appearance?

quadratus_femoris.title: Quadratus femoris
quadratus_femoris.overview: A short deep muscle caudal to the hip.
quadratus_femoris.location: Between proximal ischium and caudal proximal femur, ventral to the obturator/gemelli region.
quadratus_femoris.attachments: Ventral ischial surface to proximal caudal femur near the intertrochanteric region.
quadratus_femoris.function: Extends and laterally rotates the hip.
quadratus_femoris.physio: Distinguish it from quadriceps femoris: similar names do not imply the same location or joint action.
quadratus_femoris.recall: Does quadratus femoris insert on the patella?

capsularis.title: Capsularis · hip-region source label
capsularis.overview: The historical label generally refers to a small articular muscle associated with a joint capsule. This mesh lies near the hip.
capsularis.location: Proximal femur/hip region in the source pose; exact segmentation is not independently verified.
capsularis.attachments: Articular hip muscles are described between the peri-acetabular region, proximal femur and capsule; exact attachment points are not assigned to this ambiguous mesh.

tibialis_cranialis.title: Cranial tibial muscle
tibialis_cranialis.overview: A cranial crural muscle whose tendon reaches the medial hindpaw.
tibialis_cranialis.location: Cranial/lateral proximal tibia, with tendon crossing the dorsal tarsus obliquely.
tibialis_cranialis.attachments: Proximal lateral tibia to proximal medial metatarsal region.
tibialis_cranialis.function: Flexes the tarsus and contributes to medial rotation of the paw.
tibialis_cranialis.physio: Distinguish tarsal flexion from stifle extension; the muscle originates below the stifle.
tibialis_cranialis.recall: Which caudal crural muscle provides a strong opposing tarsal action?

extensor_digitorum_longus.title: Long digital extensor · hindlimb
extensor_digitorum_longus.overview: A long tendon-bearing muscle spanning the stifle and tarsus to the digits.
extensor_digitorum_longus.location: Craniolateral crus; tendon passes through the extensor groove near the proximal tibia and across the dorsal tarsus.
extensor_digitorum_longus.attachments: Extensor fossa of femur to extensor processes of distal phalanges II–V.
extensor_digitorum_longus.function: Extends the digits and flexes the tarsus.
extensor_digitorum_longus.physio: Its femoral origin and long distal tendons distinguish it from the cranial tibial muscle beside it.
extensor_digitorum_longus.recall: Which bone contains its proximal extensor fossa?

extensor_digitorum_lateralis.title: Lateral digital extensor · hindlimb
extensor_digitorum_lateralis.overview: A lateral crural extensor serving the lateral digit.
extensor_digitorum_lateralis.location: Lateral crus near the fibula; tendon continues onto the dorsolateral hindpaw.
extensor_digitorum_lateralis.attachments: Proximal fibula to the extensor apparatus of digit V.
extensor_digitorum_lateralis.function: Extends the lateral digit and assists tarsal flexion.
extensor_digitorum_lateralis.physio: Differentiate it from the similarly named forelimb muscle; the distal distribution is not identical.
extensor_digitorum_lateralis.recall: Which digit is lateral in the canine hindpaw?

peroneus_longus.title: Fibularis longus
peroneus_longus.overview: Also called peroneus longus; a lateral crural muscle with a tendon crossing toward the plantar foot.
peroneus_longus.location: Lateral proximal crus, passing around the lateral tarsus toward plantar attachments.
peroneus_longus.attachments: Proximal tibial/fibular and adjacent lateral joint region to plantar tarsal/metatarsal structures.
peroneus_longus.function: Flexes the tarsus and rotates the paw medially.
peroneus_longus.physio: Trace the change in tendon direction around the tarsus; a straight-line sketch can misrepresent its action.
peroneus_longus.recall: What is the modern synonym for peroneus?

peroneus_brevis.title: Fibularis brevis
peroneus_brevis.overview: A small lateral crural muscle with a shorter course than fibularis longus.
peroneus_brevis.location: Along distal lateral fibula, deep to more superficial lateral crural structures.
peroneus_brevis.attachments: Distal fibula to proximal metatarsal V.
peroneus_brevis.function: Flexes the tarsus and contributes to lateral paw control.
peroneus_brevis.physio: Use its insertion on metatarsal V to distinguish it from digital extensors continuing to the phalanges.
peroneus_brevis.recall: Does this tendon terminate on a metatarsal or a distal phalanx?

gastrocnemius.title: Gastrocnemius
gastrocnemius.overview: A two-headed caudal crural muscle forming a major component of the common calcanean tendon.
gastrocnemius.location: Caudal crus, superficial to deeper flexor structures; heads arise around the distal femur and fabellae.
gastrocnemius.attachments: Medial and lateral supracondylar regions of femur to calcaneal tuber.
gastrocnemius.function: Extends the tarsus and assists stifle flexion.
gastrocnemius.physio: Study the common calcanean tendon as a composite structure rather than assuming every strand belongs to gastrocnemius.
gastrocnemius.recall: Which two joints does this muscle cross?

flexor_digitorum_superficialis_hind.title: Superficial digital flexor · hindlimb
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_hind.overview: A multi-joint flexor with an important calcaneal attachment before its tendons reach the digits.
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_hind.location: Caudal crus, associated with gastrocnemius; tendon forms a cap over the calcaneal tuber.
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_hind.attachments: Distal caudal femur to calcaneal tuber and middle phalanges II–V.
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_hind.function: Flexes the digits and stifle, and extends/supports the tarsus.
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_hind.physio: Unlike the forelimb counterpart, it has a calcaneal relationship and crosses the stifle. Similar names do not imply identical mechanics.
flexor_digitorum_superficialis_hind.recall: Which intermediate attachment distinguishes this muscle from the forelimb superficial flexor?

flexor_digitorum_profundus_hind.title: Deep digital flexor · hindlimb
flexor_digitorum_profundus_hind.overview: A deep caudal crural flexor complex, conventionally described through medial and lateral digital-flexor components.
flexor_digitorum_profundus_hind.location: Deep caudal crus; tendons pass on the plantar tarsus and continue down the digits.
flexor_digitorum_profundus_hind.attachments: Caudal tibia/fibula and interosseous region to flexor surfaces of distal phalanges.
flexor_digitorum_profundus_hind.function: Flexes the digits and assists tarsal extension.
flexor_digitorum_profundus_hind.physio: Differentiate its distal-phalanx insertion from the superficial flexor’s middle-phalanx insertion. Source fragments do not reliably identify every component head.
flexor_digitorum_profundus_hind.recall: Which joint in a digit is directly influenced by attachment to the distal phalanx?

tibialis_caudalis.title: Caudal tibial component · source label
tibialis_caudalis.overview: This label needs species qualification: a separate caudal tibial muscle is emphasized in cats, whereas canine descriptions incorporate this region into the deep digital-flexor complex.
tibialis_caudalis.location: Deep caudal crus between or associated with digital-flexor components.
tibialis_caudalis.attachments: The source does not securely establish a separate canine origin and insertion; study the surrounding tibial/fibular flexor complex instead.
tibialis_caudalis.function: The canine parent complex flexes digits and assists tarsal extension. A feline-specific independent action is not assigned to this piece.
tibialis_caudalis.nerve: Tibial nerve supplies the caudal crural flexor group.
tibialis_caudalis.physio: This is a model-label limitation, not evidence for an extra independently testable canine muscle.
tibialis_caudalis.recall: Why must species be checked before using a comparative anatomy label?

popliteus.title: Popliteus
popliteus.overview: A short, deep muscle immediately caudal to the stifle.
popliteus.location: Spans the caudal proximal tibia, deep to gastrocnemius and the larger caudal crural muscles.
popliteus.attachments: Lateral femoral condylar region through its tendon to proximal caudomedial tibia.
popliteus.function: Rotates the tibia medially relative to the femur and contributes to stifle flexion/stability.
popliteus.physio: Its oblique course is important for rotational control; flexion-extension alone does not describe all stifle mechanics.
popliteus.recall: Why is its tibial line of pull oblique rather than straight down the crus?

ribcage.title: Rib cage and thoracic vertebral complex
ribcage.overview: A grouped axial mesh rather than one bone. It combines structures that normally move at several separate joints.
ribcage.location: Thorax, surrounding the chest cavity and bridging cervical and lumbar regions.
ribcage.attachments: Ribs articulate dorsally with thoracic vertebrae; costal cartilages connect most ribs ventrally to the sternum, while the last rib pair is floating.
ribcage.function: Protects thoracic organs, supports muscle attachments and changes shape during breathing. Grouping hides individual joint motion.
ribcage.nerve: Periosteum and joints have regional sensory innervation; intercostal nerves run in the thoracic wall.
ribcage.physio: Do not interpret one rigid mesh as proof that the living rib cage is rigid. Individual thoracic joints cannot be isolated in this grouped asset.
ribcage.recall: Which articulations allow rib movement during inspiration?

atlas.title: Atlas · C1
atlas.overview: The first cervical vertebra, specialized for supporting the skull. Unlike a typical vertebra, it has a ring-like form without a conventional body.
atlas.location: Between occipital condyles of the skull and axis.
atlas.attachments: Cranially articulates with occipital condyles; caudally with axis. The dens of axis projects into the atlas ring.
atlas.function: Atlanto-occipital motion permits head flexion/extension; atlanto-axial relationships permit rotation.
atlas.nerve: Upper cervical spinal nerves and adjacent neural tissues are related to this region; vertebra C1 is not itself a nerve.
atlas.physio: Learn the wings and arches before interpreting neck attachments. The model does not demonstrate ligament integrity or safe motion limits.
atlas.recall: Which articulation is primarily associated with nodding?

axis.title: Axis · C2
axis.overview: The second cervical vertebra, recognized by its dens and prominent spinous process.
axis.location: Immediately caudal to atlas in the cranial neck.
axis.attachments: Dens participates in the atlanto-axial articulation; caudally C2 articulates with C3. Numerous suboccipital muscles attach here.
axis.function: Provides the pivot for much of cranial-neck rotation and anchorage for head-positioning structures.
axis.nerve: Related to upper cervical neural tissues; motor innervation belongs to the surrounding muscles, not the vertebra.
axis.physio: Distinguish the dens from the spinous process. Their different positions explain different joint and muscle relationships.
axis.recall: Which muscle links the axis spine to the atlas wing?

cervical.title: Typical cervical vertebra · C3–C5 region
cervical.overview: A cervical vertebra with a body, vertebral arch, articular processes and transverse processes.
cervical.location: Mid-neck, between the specialized atlas/axis and caudal cervical transition.
cervical.attachments: Adjacent bodies are connected by intervertebral discs; articular processes form paired synovial joints. Muscles and ligaments attach to the processes.
cervical.function: Supports head/neck motion while protecting the vertebral canal and distributing load between segments.
cervical.nerve: Cervical nerves exit in relation to intervertebral foramina. Dogs have seven cervical vertebrae but eight cervical spinal nerve pairs.
cervical.physio: A vertebral label is not a spinal cord segment or nerve-root label. Assess relative orientation without inferring clinical range from mesh geometry.
cervical.recall: How do disc and articular-process joints differ?

c6.title: Cervical vertebra C6
c6.overview: A caudal cervical vertebra distinguished by its large ventral laminae on the transverse processes.
c6.location: Near the base of the neck, between C5 and C7.
c6.attachments: Articulates with neighboring cervical bodies and facets; ventral/lateral processes provide prominent muscular attachment areas.
c6.function: Supports and guides lower-neck motion and provides anchorage for hypaxial structures.
c6.nerve: Cervical spinal nerves and brachial-plexus origins are nearby; bone level alone does not identify a nerve lesion.
c6.physio: Use the ventral lamina as an identification landmark, not the size of a generic spinous process.
c6.recall: What feature helps distinguish C6 from neighboring cervical vertebrae?

c7.title: Cervical vertebra C7
c7.overview: The last cervical vertebra, forming the transition to the thoracic region.
c7.location: Caudal neck immediately cranial to T1 and the first ribs.
c7.attachments: Articulates with C6 and T1 and participates in the first-rib articulation; has a relatively prominent spinous process.
c7.function: Transfers load between mobile neck and rib-associated thorax.
c7.nerve: Cervical/cranial thoracic neural structures lie nearby; vertebral numbering does not replace nerve-root anatomy.
c7.physio: Study the cervicothoracic junction as a regional transition. The adjacent thoracic elements are grouped in this atlas.
c7.recall: What bony thoracic structure starts articulating in this transition region?

lumbar.title: Lumbar vertebra
lumbar.overview: A load-bearing vertebra with substantial body and transverse processes supporting the trunk.
lumbar.location: Between thorax and sacrum, deep to epaxial muscles and dorsal to hypaxial muscles.
lumbar.attachments: Adjacent vertebral bodies meet through discs; articular processes form paired joints. L7 meets the sacrum at the lumbosacral junction.
lumbar.function: Supports trunk loads and permits controlled spinal motion while enclosing the vertebral canal.
lumbar.nerve: Lumbar vertebral levels do not directly equal spinal cord segments; caudal roots travel within the canal before exiting.
lumbar.physio: The relationship between bone, cord and nerve roots is essential for anatomy revision. The model contains bones and muscles, not a complete neural canal dissection.
lumbar.recall: Why can a lumbar vertebra overlie a more caudal spinal cord segment?

caudal.title: Caudal vertebra
caudal.overview: One element of the tail skeleton. Proximal caudal vertebrae retain more processes; distal elements become simpler.
caudal.location: In the tail, caudal to the sacrum.
caudal.attachments: Adjacent caudal vertebrae connect through discs and, proximally, articular structures; tail muscles and connective tissues attach around them.
caudal.function: Supports tail positioning and movement. Tail length, shape and vertebral number vary across dogs.
caudal.nerve: Caudal spinal nerves supply tail tissues, but a Ca mesh number is not a matching nerve-pair number.
caudal.physio: Compare proximal and distal shapes without treating this model’s 21 pieces as a universal canine total.
caudal.recall: How does a proximal tail vertebra differ from a distal one?

sacrum.title: Sacrum
sacrum.overview: A fused axial structure formed from three sacral vertebrae in the typical adult dog.
sacrum.location: Between the two sides of the pelvis, caudal to L7 and cranial to the tail.
sacrum.attachments: Auricular surfaces articulate with ilia at sacroiliac joints; cranially meets L7 and caudally the first caudal vertebra.
sacrum.function: Transfers load between vertebral column and pelvic limbs and provides attachment for pelvic/tail structures.
sacrum.nerve: Sacral foramina transmit nerve branches; sacral bone and sacral spinal cord segments are not in identical locations.
sacrum.physio: Distinguish the sacroiliac joints from the lumbosacral joint. Their anatomy and mechanical roles differ.
sacrum.recall: Which sacral surface articulates with the ilium?

pelvis.title: Pelvis · grouped hip bones
pelvis.overview: The source groups the pelvic girdle. Each hip bone is formed chiefly by ilium, ischium and pubis meeting at the acetabulum.
pelvis.location: Caudal trunk, surrounding the pelvic cavity and lateral to sacrum.
pelvis.attachments: Sacroiliac joints link to the sacrum; acetabula receive femoral heads; left and right sides meet ventrally at the pelvic symphysis.
pelvis.function: Transfers load to the trunk, protects pelvic structures and provides broad origins for hip and pelvic-diaphragm muscles.
pelvis.nerve: Regional nerves pass through and around the pelvis; the bone itself receives sensory, not muscle-motor, innervation.
pelvis.physio: Learn iliac crest, ischiatic tuberosity and acetabulum separately even though they cannot be selected independently in this mesh.
pelvis.recall: Which three bones contribute to the acetabular region?

scapula.title: Scapula
scapula.overview: The flat shoulder blade, suspended against the trunk by muscles rather than a conventional bony joint with the rib cage.
scapula.location: Lateral cranial thorax, proximal to humerus.
scapula.attachments: Glenoid cavity articulates with humeral head. Spine, acromion, fossae and borders provide extensive muscle attachments.
scapula.function: Transfers load through the muscular sling and supplies a mobile base for the forelimb.
scapula.nerve: Suprascapular and other regional nerves run near it; bone/periosteum has local sensory supply.
scapula.physio: Separate scapulothoracic movement from shoulder-joint movement. Both can contribute to the position of the paw.
scapula.recall: Which scapular surface receives serratus ventralis?

humerus.title: Humerus
humerus.overview: The long bone of the arm, between shoulder and elbow. It is not a forearm bone.
humerus.location: Brachium, distal to scapula and proximal to radius/ulna.
humerus.attachments: Head articulates with glenoid cavity; distal condyle articulates with radius and ulna. Tubercles, crest and epicondyles anchor many muscles.
humerus.function: Acts as a lever and load-bearing link between shoulder and elbow.
humerus.nerve: Radial nerve curves around the humeral region; other major limb nerves course medially. Periosteal innervation is sensory.
humerus.physio: Trace the shoulder muscles to proximal landmarks and elbow/forearm muscles to distal landmarks.
humerus.recall: Which projection gives triceps leverage on the adjacent ulna rather than the humerus?

radius.title: Radius
radius.overview: The principal cranial weight-bearing bone of the canine forearm.
radius.location: Between humerus and carpus, paired with the ulna.
radius.attachments: Proximal head participates in the elbow; distal radius articulates with the carpus. Radioulnar connections permit limited forearm rotation.
radius.function: Transmits load and provides muscle attachment while cooperating with the ulna in forearm motion.
radius.nerve: Radial/median and other regional nerves are nearby; a bone name does not identify its entire sensory territory.
radius.physio: Distinguish radial bone anatomy from radial nerve function. Those are related regional subjects, not interchangeable labels.
radius.recall: What muscle occupies much of the space between radius and ulna?

ulna.title: Ulna
ulna.overview: The caudal forearm bone with the prominent proximal olecranon.
ulna.location: Along the radius from elbow to lateral distal forearm.
ulna.attachments: Trochlear notch articulates with humerus; distal styloid region relates to carpal bones and radius. Olecranon receives elbow extensor attachments.
ulna.function: Guides the elbow and provides a lever for triceps and other extensors.
ulna.nerve: Ulnar and other regional nerves course nearby, but the bone itself has sensory periosteal innervation.
ulna.physio: Use the olecranon to understand the elbow extensor moment arm; it is not the same landmark as the accessory carpal bone.
ulna.recall: Which notch receives the humeral trochlear surface?

femur.title: Femur
femur.overview: The long bone of the thigh, linking hip and stifle.
femur.attachments: Femoral head articulates with acetabulum; condyles meet tibia; trochlea guides patella. Trochanters provide important hip-muscle attachments.
femur.function: Transfers load and acts as a lever for hip and stifle muscle groups.
femur.nerve: Major femoral and sciatic pathways lie in the surrounding region; periosteum and joints receive sensory branches.
femur.physio: Distinguish the greater trochanter from the femoral head and the trochlea from the condyles.

fabella.title: Gastrocnemius fabella · source piece
fabella.overview: A sesamoid in the proximal gastrocnemius region, rather than an additional femoral shaft fragment. Source numbering does not identify the head with certainty.
fabella.location: Caudal to the distal femoral condyles, within the origins of gastrocnemius heads.
fabella.attachments: Associated with gastrocnemius tendinous origins and the caudal femoral articular region.
fabella.function: Alters tendon contact/force transmission and protects local tendon relationships around the stifle.
fabella.nerve: Sesamoids and neighboring tissues receive sensory supply; gastrocnemius motor innervation is tibial.
fabella.physio: Recognize sesamoids as normal anatomical structures and avoid counting them as arbitrary loose bodies.
fabella.recall: Which muscle is associated with the paired femoral fabellae?

patella.title: Patella
patella.overview: A sesamoid bone within the quadriceps extensor apparatus.
patella.location: Cranial stifle, over the femoral trochlea.
patella.attachments: Quadriceps tendon attaches proximally; patellar ligament continues distally to tibial tuberosity. Articulates with femoral trochlea.
patella.function: Redirects quadriceps force and improves the stifle extension lever arm.
patella.nerve: Regional articular/periosteal sensory supply; the motor nerve of quadriceps is femoral.
patella.physio: Patellar tracking depends on the whole extensor mechanism and limb alignment, not just the shape of the patella in isolation.
patella.recall: Which structure connects patella to tibia?

tibia.title: Tibia
tibia.overview: The main weight-bearing bone of the crus.
tibia.location: Between stifle and tarsus, medial to fibula.
tibia.attachments: Proximal condyles articulate with femur through menisci; distal cochlea articulates with talus. Tibial tuberosity receives the patellar ligament.
tibia.function: Transmits load and provides leverage/attachments for stifle and distal-limb muscles.
tibia.nerve: Tibial nerve is a nearby nerve, not the name of all sensory innervation to the bone.
tibia.physio: Relate tibial tuberosity to quadriceps force transmission. The menisci and cruciate ligaments are not separately modeled here.
tibia.recall: Which missing soft tissues normally sit between tibial and femoral joint surfaces?

fibula.title: Fibula
fibula.overview: A slender lateral crural bone, distinct from the principal weight-bearing tibia.
fibula.location: Lateral to tibia from the proximal crus to the lateral tarsus.
fibula.attachments: Proximal and distal relationships with tibia; distal end forms the lateral malleolus and participates in tarsal stability.
fibula.function: Provides muscle attachments and lateral distal-limb support.
fibula.nerve: Fibular nerve passes near the proximal lateral crus; periosteal innervation is sensory.
fibula.physio: Separate the common fibular nerve from the fibula itself. Their nearby courses matter, but they are different structures.
fibula.recall: Which distal landmark is formed by the fibula?

calcaneus.title: Calcaneus · calcaneal tuber region
calcaneus.overview: The source emphasizes the calcaneal tuber, the projecting heel region of the proximal tarsus.
calcaneus.location: Caudoproximal tarsus, plantar to much of the talus.
calcaneus.attachments: Common calcanean tendon attaches to the tuber; the calcaneus articulates with adjacent tarsal bones and supports deep flexor tendon passage medially.
calcaneus.function: Provides a substantial lever for tarsal extension and guides tendon force transmission.
calcaneus.nerve: Local sensory supply to bone and periarticular tissues; it has no motor action of its own.
calcaneus.physio: Distinguish the heel/tuber from the tarsocrural joint axis. The lever distance helps explain gastrocnemius mechanics.
calcaneus.recall: Which composite tendon inserts at this landmark?

talus.title: Talus · tibial tarsal bone
talus.overview: A proximal tarsal bone forming the principal hinge-like articulation with the tibia.
talus.attachments: Trochlea articulates with distal tibia; distal head relates to the central tarsal bone and adjacent tarsal surfaces.
talus.function: Receives crural load and guides tarsocrural flexion/extension.
talus.nerve: Regional joint/periosteal sensory nerves; no skeletal-muscle motor supply.
talus.physio: Separate talar trochlea from calcaneal tuber. One is an articular surface, the other an extensor lever.
talus.recall: Which bone forms the opposing surface to the talar trochlea?

central_tarsal.title: Central tarsal bone
central_tarsal.overview: A small bone in the middle tarsal row.
central_tarsal.location: Distal to talus and proximal to much of the distal tarsal row.
central_tarsal.attachments: Articulates with talus and neighboring distal tarsal bones, constrained by short ligaments.
central_tarsal.function: Transfers load through the compact tarsal column; its local movements are much smaller than the main tarsocrural hinge.
central_tarsal.physio: The tarsus contains multiple joints. Do not apply the large motion seen at the tibia–talus joint to every small tarsal articulation.
central_tarsal.recall: Which proximal tarsal bone lies mainly above it?

tarsal_i.title: First tarsal bone
tarsal_i.overview: The medial member of the distal tarsal row.
tarsal_i.location: Medial distal tarsus near the proximal metatarsal region.
tarsal_i.attachments: Contacts neighboring tarsal and medial metatarsal structures through small joints and short ligaments.
tarsal_i.function: Helps form the stable medial tarsal column and provides local soft-tissue attachment.
tarsal_i.physio: Its numeral names the tarsal bone, not the same-numbered digit. Keep row and side orientation clear.
tarsal_i.recall: Is the first tarsal bone on the medial or lateral side?

tarsal_ii.title: Second tarsal bone
tarsal_ii.overview: A small bone of the distal tarsal row.
tarsal_ii.location: Medial/intermediate distal tarsus, beside the first and third tarsal bones.
tarsal_ii.attachments: Proximally relates to the central tarsal region and distally to the second metatarsal column.
tarsal_ii.function: Distributes compressive load within the distal tarsus while short ligaments limit excessive movement.
tarsal_ii.nerve: Local sensory innervation of periosteum and adjacent joints.
tarsal_ii.physio: Isolate it to learn the compact distal row, then restore neighboring bones before interpreting loading.
tarsal_ii.recall: Which tarsal row contains this bone?

tarsal_iii.title: Third tarsal bone
tarsal_iii.overview: A distal-row tarsal bone in the central load-transfer region of the hindpaw.
tarsal_iii.location: Distal to central tarsal bone, proximal to the third metatarsal region.
tarsal_iii.attachments: Articulates with neighboring tarsal bones and the third metatarsal column.
tarsal_iii.function: Transfers load from proximal tarsal structures to the metatarsus.
tarsal_iii.physio: Compare its compact shape with the elongated metatarsal beneath it. They have different structural roles.
tarsal_iii.recall: Which bone lies mainly proximal to it?

tarsal_iv.title: Fourth tarsal bone
tarsal_iv.overview: An elongated lateral tarsal bone spanning the height of more than one medial row.
tarsal_iv.location: Lateral tarsus, distal to calcaneus and proximal to lateral metatarsals.
tarsal_iv.attachments: Articulates with calcaneus, adjacent central/distal tarsal bones and lateral metatarsal columns.
tarsal_iv.function: Supports the lateral tarsal column and helps distribute forces toward the lateral hindpaw.
tarsal_iv.physio: Its height is useful for identifying the lateral side in an isolated tarsal view.
tarsal_iv.recall: Why does it look taller than the second or third tarsal bone?

metatarsal.title: Metatarsal · source-numbered piece
metatarsal.overview: An elongated hindpaw bone between the tarsus and digits. The source uses four mesh numbers that are not verified anatomical digit numerals.
metatarsal.location: Distal to tarsus and proximal to hindpaw phalanges.
metatarsal.attachments: Proximal base articulates with tarsal/neighboring metatarsal bones; distal head articulates with a proximal phalanx and sesamoid apparatus.
metatarsal.function: Transfers load along the hindpaw and provides attachment/support for tendons and intrinsic paw tissues.
metatarsal.nerve: Digital and regional periosteal/articular sensory branches; no motor supply.
metatarsal.physio: Do not rename source piece 1 as metatarsal I. Dogs typically bear weight through digits II–V, and source indexing can differ.
metatarsal.recall: What evidence would confirm the anatomical digit corresponding to a mesh number?

hind_digit_piece.title: Hindpaw digital bone · numbered source piece
hind_digit_piece.overview: A piece from the hindpaw digital skeleton. The source does not consistently resolve phalanx level versus small sesamoid pieces.
hind_digit_piece.location: At the distal hindpaw beyond the metatarsal region.
hind_digit_piece.attachments: The digital apparatus includes phalanges, joints and sesamoids with flexor/extensor attachments; precise articulations depend on this piece’s confirmed identity.
hind_digit_piece.function: Digital bones transmit load and provide tendon levers; an exact insertion or joint level is not assigned from ambiguous numbering.
hind_digit_piece.nerve: Digital sensory branches serve the regional bone/joint tissues.
hind_digit_piece.physio: Use its position among neighboring pieces for orientation, but confirm digit and level in a labeled canine reference before memorizing them.
hind_digit_piece.recall: Is the selected shape a long phalanx or a small sesamoid-like piece? What would confirm it?

accessory_carpal.title: Accessory carpal bone
accessory_carpal.overview: A projecting proximal-row carpal bone important for tendon leverage.
accessory_carpal.location: Palmarolateral carpus, behind the main carpal column.
accessory_carpal.attachments: Articulates with ulnar-side carpal/distal forearm structures; receives flexor carpi ulnaris and ulnaris lateralis attachments.
accessory_carpal.function: Provides a lever and attachment platform for carpal support and flexor forces.
accessory_carpal.nerve: Local periosteal and articular sensory branches; no motor function.
accessory_carpal.physio: This is the prominent palmar carpal landmark, not a forelimb equivalent of the olecranon’s location.
accessory_carpal.recall: Which carpal flexor terminates on this bone?

ulnar_carpal.title: Ulnar carpal bone
ulnar_carpal.overview: The lateral main bone of the proximal carpal row.
ulnar_carpal.location: Lateral proximal carpus, beside the radial/intermedioradial carpal region and near accessory carpal.
ulnar_carpal.attachments: Contacts distal ulna and adjacent carpal bones.
ulnar_carpal.function: Distributes load through the lateral carpus and supports joint alignment.
ulnar_carpal.physio: Compare row position before interpreting carpal flexion; the antebrachiocarpal joint differs from the smaller intercarpal joints.
ulnar_carpal.recall: Which forearm bone is associated with its name?

radial_carpal.title: Unnumbered carpal piece
radial_carpal.overview: The source calls this piece Carpal without a reliable anatomical qualifier. It lies in the proximal carpal region, but a precise identity is not asserted.
radial_carpal.location: Forepaw carpal complex between forearm and metacarpus.
radial_carpal.attachments: The canine proximal row includes intermedioradial, ulnar and accessory carpal elements; exact contacts depend on which element this mesh represents.
radial_carpal.function: Contributes to load transmission and coordinated carpal motion.
radial_carpal.nerve: Regional periosteal and articular sensory supply.
radial_carpal.physio: Avoid treating the technical profile name as confirmation of an intermedioradial bone. The visible source-identity warning takes precedence.
radial_carpal.recall: Which labeled neighboring bones would help confirm this piece?

carpal_sesamoid.title: Carpal sesamoid · unspecified
carpal_sesamoid.overview: A small sesamoid-associated piece identified only generally by the source.
carpal_sesamoid.location: Around the carpal region, associated with local tendon/ligament mechanics.
carpal_sesamoid.attachments: Sesamoids develop within tendinous or related tissues; the exact tendon and articular contacts are not verified for this mesh.
carpal_sesamoid.function: Redirects or distributes local tendon forces according to its actual position.
carpal_sesamoid.nerve: Local sensory supply; a sesamoid is not a contractile muscle.
carpal_sesamoid.physio: Do not give an unspecified sesamoid a named tendon attachment solely from its size or appearance.
carpal_sesamoid.recall: What surrounding tendon would you need to identify first?

carpal_i.title: First carpal bone
carpal_i.overview: The small medial member of the distal carpal row.
carpal_i.location: Medial distal carpus, proximal to the first metacarpal region.
carpal_i.attachments: Articulates with neighboring carpal structures and metacarpal I.
carpal_i.function: Forms part of the medial carpal support column and the skeletal base of the dewclaw region.
carpal_i.physio: Separate carpal I from metacarpal I and digit I: these describe successive levels, not interchangeable structures.
carpal_i.recall: What lies distal to the first carpal bone?

carpal_ii.title: Second carpal bone
carpal_ii.overview: A distal-row carpal bone associated with the second metacarpal column.
carpal_ii.location: Distal carpus, lateral to carpal I and medial to carpal III.
carpal_ii.attachments: Proximal carpal surfaces and distal metacarpal II, with adjacent intercarpal contacts.
carpal_ii.function: Transfers load through a compact joint network constrained by short ligaments.
carpal_ii.nerve: Regional periosteal and articular sensory nerves.
carpal_ii.physio: Use neighboring numerals to establish orientation rather than treating each small bone as a freely moving hinge.
carpal_ii.recall: Which numbered metacarpal is its principal distal neighbor?

carpal_iii.title: Third carpal bone
carpal_iii.overview: A distal-row carpal bone over the central forepaw region.
carpal_iii.location: Between second and fourth carpal bones, proximal to metacarpal III.
carpal_iii.attachments: Proximal-row carpal structures and the third metacarpal column.
carpal_iii.function: Shares load transfer through the distal carpus and stabilizes the metacarpal base.
carpal_iii.physio: Compare its block-like form with the shaft of metacarpal III; compact shape helps the carpal cluster distribute loads.
carpal_iii.recall: Is this a proximal-row or distal-row carpal bone?

carpal_iv.title: Fourth carpal bone
carpal_iv.overview: The lateral distal-row carpal bone supporting the lateral metacarpal region.
carpal_iv.location: Distal lateral carpus, medial to the projecting accessory carpal region.
carpal_iv.attachments: Proximal carpal structures and lateral metacarpal columns, principally IV and V.
carpal_iv.function: Distributes load into the lateral forepaw while local ligaments limit excessive displacement.
carpal_iv.nerve: Local periosteal and articular sensory branches.
carpal_iv.physio: Distinguish the lateral distal-row block from accessory carpal, which projects palmarly and serves as a tendon lever.
carpal_iv.recall: Which carpal bone projects behind the main column?

metacarpal.title: Metacarpal bone
metacarpal.overview: An elongated forepaw bone joining the carpus to a digit. The source provides a Roman-numeral identity for most pieces.
metacarpal.location: Between distal carpal row and proximal phalanges.
metacarpal.attachments: Proximal base articulates with carpal/neighboring metacarpal bones; distal head meets a proximal phalanx and sesamoid apparatus.
metacarpal.function: Transmits paw load and supports digital tendon/intrinsic-muscle relationships. Digit I differs from the principal weight-bearing II–V set.
metacarpal.nerve: Digital/regional periosteal and articular sensory branches.
metacarpal.physio: Treat extra source pieces with the same numeral as duplicate portions until anatomical segmentation is verified.
metacarpal.recall: Which numeral corresponds to the medial dewclaw region?

proximal_phalanx.title: Proximal phalanx · forepaw
proximal_phalanx.overview: The first phalanx of a digit; the source misspells proximalis in several labels.
proximal_phalanx.location: Immediately distal to the metacarpal head.
proximal_phalanx.attachments: Proximally forms the metacarpophalangeal joint; distally usually meets a middle phalanx. Digit I is an exception with only proximal and distal phalanges.
proximal_phalanx.function: Transfers load and forms a lever within the digital flexor/extensor apparatus.
proximal_phalanx.nerve: Digital sensory nerves supply periosteal and joint tissues.
proximal_phalanx.physio: Learn digit-specific exceptions instead of assuming every digit has three phalanges. The source numeral is shown in the model note.
proximal_phalanx.recall: Which forepaw digit lacks a middle phalanx?

middle_phalanx.title: Middle phalanx · forepaw
middle_phalanx.overview: The intermediate phalanx of one of the main digits.
middle_phalanx.location: Between proximal and distal phalanges in digits II–V.
middle_phalanx.attachments: Articulates with proximal and distal phalanges; receives superficial digital-flexor attachment.
middle_phalanx.function: Participates in digital flexion/extension and transmits load toward the distal digit.
middle_phalanx.physio: Contrast the superficial flexor insertion here with the deep flexor insertion on the distal phalanx.
middle_phalanx.recall: Which digital flexor reaches the middle rather than distal phalanx?

distal_phalanx.title: Distal phalanx · forepaw
distal_phalanx.overview: The terminal bone of a digit, supporting the claw apparatus.
distal_phalanx.location: Distal end of the digit, within tissues surrounding the claw.
distal_phalanx.attachments: Articulates proximally with the middle phalanx, or proximal phalanx in digit I; receives terminal flexor and extensor attachments.
distal_phalanx.function: Supports the claw and provides opposing tendon lever points for distal digital motion.
distal_phalanx.nerve: Regional digital sensory branches; pain sensation depends on living surrounding tissues, not the mesh surface.
distal_phalanx.physio: A bone-only view omits the claw sheath, pads and many soft-tissue constraints. Do not infer weight-contact shape from bone alone.
distal_phalanx.recall: Which flexor tendon reaches its flexor surface?

skull.title: Skull · grouped cranial and facial bones
skull.overview: A merged skeletal representation of the head, combining bones that normally have distinct names and sutures.
skull.location: Rostral to atlas, surrounding the braincase, orbits and nasal/oral regions.
skull.attachments: Occipital condyles articulate with atlas; temporal regions form the mandibular articulations. Numerous cranial and facial surfaces anchor muscles.
skull.function: Protects sensory/neural structures and provides the framework for feeding, breathing and head support.
skull.nerve: Cranial nerves pass through named foramina, but those pathways and individual bones are not separately segmented in this mesh.
skull.physio: Learn grouped-model limits: selecting Skull is not selecting a single anatomical bone. Use the reference to identify the occipital, temporal and facial regions.
skull.recall: Which part articulates with atlas, and which part participates in the jaw joint?

mandible.title: Mandible · grouped lower jaw
mandible.overview: The lower-jaw structure, with left and right sides joined at the mandibular symphysis.
mandible.location: Ventral to the facial skull, carrying the lower teeth and forming the mandibular rami caudally.
mandible.attachments: Condylar processes articulate with temporal bones; coronoid processes receive temporalis and the angular/ramus regions support other jaw muscles.
mandible.function: Acts as a lever for chewing and mouth opening while supporting lower dentition and oral-floor attachments.
mandible.nerve: Inferior alveolar branches of mandibular CN V supply regional sensation; muscle motor supply differs by attached muscle.
mandible.physio: Distinguish condylar, coronoid and angular processes. A grouped mesh does not show all tooth, periodontal or joint-disc anatomy.
mandible.recall: Which process receives temporalis and which forms the jaw articulation?
